documents/manifesto-2026-easy-read-pdf.m.text:
# Green Party Manifesto 2026: A Green government. For all of us. (Easy Read)

<!-- page 1 -->

Green Party Manifesto 2026:
A Green government. For all of us.

Published: August 2026
Authorised by Miriam Ross – greens.org.nz

<!-- page 2 -->

Before you start

This is a long document.

It can be hard for some people to
read a document this long.

Some things you can do to make it
easier are:
- read it a few pages at a time

- set aside some quiet time to look
at it

- have someone read it with you to
support you to understand it.

1

<!-- page 3 -->

What you will find in here

Page number:

About this Easy Read ......................... 3

Why vote for the Greens? ................... 5

What will the Greens do for
disabled people? ............................... 11

Important policies for
disabled people ................................. 14

About the 2026 general election ....... 25

Contact information ........................... 32
2

<!-- page 4 -->

About this Easy Read

This Easy Read is by the Green
Party of Aotearoa New Zealand
manifesto.

The Green Party of Aotearoa New
Zealand is a political party.

A political party is a group of people
with the same ideas that want to be
part of the Government.

In this document the Green Party of
Aotearoa New Zealand will be called
the Greens.

Where it says we / us in this
document this means the Greens.
3

<!-- page 5 -->

A manifesto tells everyone what a
political party:
- believes in

- wants to happen.

You can read our full manifesto at
this website:
www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026

This website is not in Easy Read.

This Easy Read document has
information about:
- why you should vote for us

- how to vote for us.

4

<!-- page 6 -->

Why vote for the Greens?

The Greens want:
- the Government to support
people

- nature to do well.

We want everyone to have the things
they need like:
- food

- electricity / power

- housing

- transport

- doctors.

5

<!-- page 7 -->

We want to take care of the
environment which means the things
around us like:
- water

- forests

- air

- soil

- climate / weather.

We want a fair Government.

We want a Government that works
for everyone.

We do not want a Government that
just works for the people with the
most money.
6

<!-- page 8 -->

We want the Government to always
respect the rights of Māori.

Rights are things that the
law says every person should:
- have

- be able to do.

These rights were agreed on in
Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Te Tiriti o Waitangi is an important
agreement between:
- Māori
and

- the Crown / Government.

7

<!-- page 9 -->

Te Tiriti o Waitangi:
- kept Māori independent which
means they make their own
decisions

- made a government for everyone
else.

Te Tiriti o Waitangi also says the
rights of Māori are:
- all the rights everyone else has
and

- control over their:
o

lands

o

customs / ways of doing
things

o

everything else that is
important to them.
8

<!-- page 10 -->

We want the people with the most
money to pay more tax.

Tax is money that goes to the
government.

Tax is used by the government to pay
for things like:
- schools

- roads

- disability support services.

The people we want to pay more tax
are:
- big businesses

- people who are very rich.

9

<!-- page 11 -->

With the extra money from taxes we
will look after:
- people

- nature / the environment.

10

<!-- page 12 -->

What will the Greens do for disabled
people?

Disabled people are important to the
Greens.

We want disabled people to live with
dignity.

Dignity means:
- being treated with respect

- having all the things you need to
live a good life.

Disabled people should be able to
make the same choices as everyone
else.

11

<!-- page 13 -->

We want disabled whānau / families
to have good lives.

Disabled people should have the
same rights as everyone else.

Disabled people should be able to
access things like:
- transport to get the places they
want to go

- housing in the community they
want to live in.

There are lots of barriers for
disabled people.

A barrier is something that makes it
harder for you to do something.
12

<!-- page 14 -->

Things are very hard for:
- tāngata whaikaha Māori / Māori
disabled people

- disabled people who are treated
unfairly for other reasons.

The Government we have now has
made things worse.

The Greens will make sure that all
disabled people get the support they
need to be part of their communities.

We want disabled people to have
great lives.

We want to make things better for
people who face the most barriers.

13

<!-- page 15 -->

Important policies for disabled people

1. Disability rights law
We will make a strong disability
rights law which respects Te Tiriti o
Waitangi.

This law will make sure disabled
people can get easy access to:
- places

- services.

2. Support decisions
We will support disabled people to
make their own decisions about
their lives.

14

<!-- page 16 -->

3. Enough money
We will make sure disabled people
have enough money for:
- the extra things they need to
live

- medical / healthcare costs.

This money will be given to
disabled people no matter:
- how they became disabled

- who they live with.

15

<!-- page 17 -->

4. Make services better
We will improve how important
services work with disabled people
like:
- healthcare

- education

- disability services.

We will use Enabling Good Lives.

16

<!-- page 18 -->

Enabling Good Lives is a
different way of thinking about
disability support.

Enabling Good Lives is about
having:
- choice

- control

- support

- a good life.

5. Support children with
disabilities
We will make sure all children with
disabilities get the support they
need early in their lives.

17

<!-- page 19 -->

This includes:
- getting a diagnosis

- support with learning at school.

Here diagnosis means naming the
medical / learning condition
someone has after doing tests.

6. Choice of where to live
We will give disabled people real
choices about where they can live.

We will make rules that make more
accessible housing.

Accessible means something
works well for everyone including
disabled people.
18

<!-- page 20 -->

7. Easier to get around
We will make it easy for disabled
people to get around like using
public transport.

We will make Total Mobility taxis
cheaper again.

8. Good access to education after
high school
We will make sure disabled people
can access a good education after
high school.

This includes going to:
- university

- wānanga / Māori places of
learning.
19

<!-- page 21 -->

9. Jobs in the Government.
We will support disabled people to
get jobs in the Government.

We will train Government staff how
to treat disabled people in fair
ways.

10. Support for disabled people
from other countries
We will make it easier for disabled
people from other countries to live
here.

We will get rid of rules that say it
costs too much to have them here.

20

<!-- page 22 -->

11. Ban hate speech
We will make it illegal to use hate
speech that attacks someone for
things like their:
- disability

- religion

- gender.

Hate speech is saying horrible
things about someone.

Hate speech can also be:
- pictures

- writing

- on the internet.

21

<!-- page 23 -->

Hate speech can make:
- the person feel unsafe

- other people think wrong
things about the person.

Gender is if you are:
- a man

- a woman

- another gender like nonbinary.

22

<!-- page 24 -->

12. Safety plans
We will work with disabled people
on safety plans.

This includes plans for:
- •

emergencies like:
o

storms

o

earthquakes

family and sexual violence.

You can read our full disability policy
at this website:
www.greens.org.nz/disability_policy

There is a version of this full policy in
plain language.
23

<!-- page 25 -->

We have other policies for:
- people

- nature / the environment.

You can find our other policies at this
website:
www.greens.org.nz/policy

This website is not in Easy Read.

24

<!-- page 26 -->

About the 2026 general election

A general election is happening this
year.

Here a general election is when you
can vote for who you want to be in
Parliament.

Making a vote is when you choose
who you think should win an election.

Enrol to vote
You need to enrol before you can
vote.

Here enrol means you fill in a form
to add your name to the electoral
roll.

25

<!-- page 27 -->

The electoral roll is a list of all the
people in New Zealand who are
enrolled to vote.

Enrolments close on 25 October
2026.

You cannot enrol when voting starts.

You can find out more about how to
enrol:
- by phone:
0800 36 76 56

- at this website:
https://vote.nz/accessible-2026

26

<!-- page 28 -->

Voting
Voting in the general election
happens:
- from 26 October 2026

- to 7 November 2026.

You can go to any voting place in
Aotearoa New Zealand.

There will be orange signs outside a
voting place to show you where to
go.

At the voting place you will be given a
voting paper.

Here a voting paper is where you
choose who you want to vote for.
27

<!-- page 29 -->

The 2 votes you get on the voting
paper are the:
- party vote

- electorate vote for a person.

Here a party vote is choosing the
political party you want to be in
Government.

An electorate is an area of the
country set up for voting.

Each electorate has about the same
number of people in it.

Here an electorate vote is choosing
the candidate / person for your area
who you want to be in parliament.

28

<!-- page 30 -->

You can only vote for 1 party.

You can use your party vote to
support the Greens to be in
Government.

How to vote for us
1. Get your voting paper
Staff at the voting place can give
you your voting paper.

2. Party vote
Tick the circle next to the Green
Party.

This is on the left side of the paper.

29

<!-- page 31 -->

3. Electorate vote
Tick the circle next to the name of
the person you want to vote for in
your electorate.

This is on the right side of the
paper.

4. Put your voting paper in the box
Staff at the voting place can show
you the correct box to put your
voting paper in.

If you find voting hard
There are other ways to vote if you
find voting hard.

30

<!-- page 32 -->

You can ask to vote in a different way
by calling this phone number:
0800 36 76 56

You can also find more information
about the 2026 general election in
the Easy Read called Get ready to
enrol and vote in the 2026 General
Election.

You can find this Easy Read at:
https://vote.nz/accessible-2026

31

<!-- page 33 -->

Contact information

You can phone the Greens on:
04 801 5102

This number may cost you money to
call.

You can email the Greens at:
green.party@greens.org.nz

You can visit our website:
www.greens.org.nz

This website is not in Easy Read.

32

<!-- page 34 -->

This information has been written by the Green
Party of Aotearoa New Zealand.

It has been translated into Easy Read by the
Make it Easy Kia Māmā Mai service of People
First New Zealand Ngā Tāngata Tuatahi.

The ideas in this document are not the ideas of
People First New Zealand Ngā Tāngata Tuatahi.

All images used in this Easy Read document are
subject to copyright rules and cannot be used
without permission.

Make it Easy uses images from:
• Photosymbols
• Change Images
• Huriana Kopeke-Te Aho
• SGC Image Works
• T Wood
• Studio Rebeko
• Inga Kramer.

33

documents/manifesto-2026-full-pdf.md.text:
# Green Party Manifesto 2026 — A Green government. For all of us. (full PDF)

<!-- page 1 -->

MANIFESTO
THE GREEN PARTY

20
26

<!-- page 2 -->

A Green government.

FOR ALL OF US.
6 Children
7 Climate action: emissions
reduction
8 Climate action: resilience and
adaptation
9 Conservation and biodiversity
10 Culture and creativity
11 Democracy
12 Digital technology
13 Disability
14 Drug law reform
15 Education
16 Energy
17 Environmental protection
18 Food, fibre and forestry
19 Freshwater
20 Gender equity
21 Global affairs and trade
22 Health
23 Housing
24 Immigration and refugees

25 Incomes
26 Justice and community
safety
27 Local government
28 Māori Centred
29 Mental health
30 Oceans and fisheries
31 Overseas New Zealanders
32 Pacific Peoples
33 Public services
34 Rainbow communities
35 Seniors
36 Small businesses
37 Te Tiriti o Waitangi
38 Tertiary education
39 Transport
40 Violence prevention
41 Welfare of animals
42 Workforce rights
43 Zero waste

Authorised by Miriam Ross, greens.org.nz

<!-- page 3 -->

Our vision is an Aotearoa that honours Te
Tiriti o Waitangi, where power and wealth sit
with our communities, and where people and
the rest of nature thrive together.
Aotearoa has enough for all of us. Our
government should work for people and
planet, not the greed of corporations and their
shareholders.

water, forests, air and soil. And real democracy,
because laws should be made for regular New
Zealanders, not those who can afford to buy
access to shape the rules in their favour.

For the past three years we’ve seen a
Government on the side of the super-rich and
the most powerful corporations.

Paid for by a plan that will tax the super-rich
and mega-corporations, help fund critical social
services, and cut income tax for 96 percent of
people.

Climate action cut, protections for nature
gutted, and decisions handed to lobbyists and
donors while families struggle with power bills,
rent and groceries.
We’ve been told our entire lives that a fairer
country is impossible by those profiting from
things staying exactly as they are: unequal and
unfair.
But New Zealanders know better. Politics
belongs to those who turn up, and in
communities across the motu, people are
turning up demanding action.
This manifesto is our plan for a Green
government to harness the energy for change,
built on three priorities: affordable living,
healthy nature and real democracy.
Affordable living, because we can have
affordable electricity, housing, transport and
groceries if we take on mega-corporate profits,
and only the Green Party are willing to do that.
Healthy nature, because since the beginning
we have worked to protect and restore our

None of this would be possible without the
hopes, ideas and passion of Green Party
members, and the movement they’ve built. This
manifesto is their work, and their commitment
to change in Aotearoa.
That change is not hypothetical. Last time the
Greens were in Government, we took more
action on climate than the previous three
decades of governments combined, secured
the biggest ever boost to funding for protecting
native plants and wildlife, and delivered
Aotearoa’s first plan to eliminate family and
sexual violence.
A party vote for the Green Party puts more
Green MPs and Ministers around the decisionmaking table to reverse the damage from the
last three years and fix the rules so they’re on
the side of people and planet.
Outlined in this document is a plan to do what
is necessary. Protect what we all love. Ensure
everyone’s needs are met. And make life better
for all of us here in Aotearoa.

Marama Davidson | Chlöe Swarbrick
Green Party Co-Leaders

<!-- page 4 -->

Thriving tamariki and rangatahi
The Green Party will work
to build a system that puts
tamariki, rangatahi and
whānau first.
Our tamariki and rangatahi deserve to be
loved, nurtured and safe. They should be
connected with their whānau, cared for and
free to express their authentic selves, no
matter where they live. We know we have
enough to ensure tamariki are free from
poverty and supported through every step
of their unique journey. Supporting tamariki
means ensuring whānau and communities
have everything they need to support their
wellbeing.
We have a shared responsibility to make
sure tamariki voices are heard, centred and
reflected in all decisions that impact them.
Tamariki deserve a skilled, well-supported
workforce that is trauma informed, culturally
responsive and properly trained.
Tamariki Māori are disproportionately
impacted by a child protection system
that excludes meaningful partnership and
underinvests in culturally grounded, whānauled solutions. A functioning system should
centre whakapapa and identity, with whānau
and hapū resourced to lead decisions
affecting their tamariki.

Children

The Green Party reflects our commitment
to Te Tiriti o Waitangi by addressing the
inequities tamariki Māori face in everyday life
and in the state care system.

6

Our plan
1. Legislate so that the child’s voice is
central in all decisions that matter
to them by using the Child Impact
Assessment Tool consistently and fully
incorporating the Rights of the Child into
legislation.
2. Increase the Best Start payment and
extend it to every child under three as a
universal child benefit for the early years.
3. Elevate workforce safety by funding
training and a workforce development
strategy prioritising Māori, Pacific,
rainbow, disabled and community
provider pathways.
4. Improve access to both diagnosis
and support services for children with
disabilities or learning support needs.
5. Amend the Oranga Tamariki Act so that
it protects tamariki Māori and explicitly
embeds whānau participation in
decision-making to exercise iwi or hapū
authority.

Climate action:
emissions reduction

Bold action and solutions that
hold polluters to account
The Green Party will drive
meaningful action, cutting
climate pollution and making
big polluters pay.
We will ensure that polluting corporations
pay for Aotearoa to electrify our economy.
By rapidly phasing out fossil fuels, we can
ease cost of living pressures and decrease
our vulnerability to global price shocks.

Our plan
1. Strengthen the Zero Carbon Act by
requiring the government Budget
process to be consistent with limiting
global warming to 1.5 degrees, gross
emissions reduction targets and
international commitments.

Under the leadership of a Green Minister
for Climate Change, emissions began to
drop. But now, the current Government is
deliberately making choices to take us off
that track. In Aotearoa, progress towards
our domestic climate targets is at risk. Our
international reputation has been tarnished
due to this Government’s decisions to
weaken our climate targets and exempt
our biggest polluters from paying for their
greenhouse gas emissions, undermining
international agreements we have signed
up to.

2. Empower the Climate Change
Commission to directly set unit supply
in the Emissions Trading Scheme, in
line with emissions budgets. Align the
government Budget process with the
National Adaptation Plan and Emissions
Reduction Plans.

Decades of climate inaction shows
that a hands-off government will fail to
decarbonise our economy and secure the
future everyone deserves. The market
will not respond to the climate crisis at the
scale or pace we need, and won’t give fair
outcomes for those most affected.

4. Reform the Emissions Trading Scheme
(ETS) to restore credibility to the market
by phasing out the free allocation of
units, removing and forestry offsetting
so the system functions as a genuine
‘cap-and-trade’ system and redirecting
funding from the reformed ETS to an
improved Government Investment in
Decarbonising Industry Fund.

We need political leadership that stops
emissions at source, makes polluters pay,
and focuses all government institutions on
limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees.
The Green Party will implement climate
solutions that tackle the root causes and
honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi. We will remove
economic incentives that encourage and
enable climate pollution.

3. Introduce a price on agricultural
emissions to ensure methane reduction
targets are met, with financial and
technical support for on-farm emissions
reduction.

5. Ensure Aotearoa meets our Paris
Agreement commitments through
strong domestic action and, if
necessary, environmentally and socially
responsible initiatives overseas.
6. Improve public transparency on the
costs of inaction by including the fiscal
impact of the Nationally Determined
Contribution obligation in the financial
statements.

Climate action: emissions reduction

Children

7

<!-- page 5 -->

Keeping Aotearoa safe and prepared

Climate action: resilience and adaptation

The Green Party will prepare
all New Zealanders for the
impacts of climate change.

8

We will ensure that everyone is
comprehensively supported through both
the transition to a zero emissions economy
and increasingly severe weather events like
cyclones.
Climate change is one of the biggest
challenges of our time. Across Aotearoa,
we are already feeling the impacts of more
intense and frequent storms, flooding and
drought with devastating consequences.
Marae and community groups are often
on the frontlines of the emergency and
clean-up response, but these groups are not
supported by the Government to proactively
plan and adapt.
People are worried about rising insurance
prices, and what happens when disaster
strikes, particularly those living in
increasingly flood and slip exposed areas.
They have not received any clarity from
the Government about help that might be
available down the track when they need it.

Our plan
1. Ensure climate adaptation planning
affirms tino rangatiratanga and upholds
the mana motuhake of whānau, hapū
and iwi over whenua, wai and taonga by
appropriately funding a Māori Climate
Resilience Fund.
2. Expand the role of the Natural Hazards
Commission to include cover for climaterelated weather events and ensure it
plays a key role in managing communityled adaptation and retreat.
3. Prioritise long-term, nature-based
solutions over short-term engineering
solutions, and increase funding for hapū,
iwi and community organisations to
deliver these.
4. Ensure planning frameworks give effect
to the need for climate adaptation in the
approach to land and water use, together
with supporting ecosystem restoration
and conservation.

Climate change means that some areas are
not safe to build in, nor to keep living in, and
so retreat is the only safe option in the long
term. But again, the Government has failed to
help communities facing this uncertain future
with any support, plans or guidance.

5. Establish a dedicated fund for central and
local government to implement climate
adaptation and resilience measures,
including funding for partnerships
with tangata whenua and community
organisations.

The Green Party will provide this muchneeded clarity.

6. Scale up support for, and work with,
neighbouring countries in the Pacific to
adapt to climate change, and advocate for
an international agreement on the rights
of people displaced by climate change

We will ensure that any National Adaptation
Framework is anchored by Te Tiriti o
Waitangi. We will support the autonomy
and self-determination of hapū, iwi and
community organisations to develop
and implement their own climate change
response plans.
The Green Party will ensure that local
government and communities are
comprehensively funded to respond to their
climate adaptation challenges.

Conservation
and biodiversity

Protecting and restoring plants,
animals and ecosystems
The Green Party will protect
our precious whenua, moana
and taonga species from
corporate exploitation.
Aotearoa is home to natural taonga found
nowhere else in the world. Our ngahere
(forests), awa (rivers) and moana are central
to our national identity and way of life.
The Luxon Government has made it easier
for corporations to plunder and tear up te
taiao (nature), putting private profits ahead
of our treasured native wildlife. Meanwhile,
many of our native species are on the brink of
collapse. Without urgent action, we’re at risk
of losing them forever.
The Green Party will work towards protecting
30% of land and oceans because we
know the mauri and health of te taiao is
foundational to the wellbeing of our people,
our climate and our communities. We will
achieve this by giving effect to Te Tiriti o
Waitangi and recognising tangata whenua as
the original and ongoing kaitiaki of Aotearoa.
New Zealanders deserve to experience our
national parks and hear the calls of our native
manu for generations to come. That’s why
the Green Party will ensure conservation
decisions are made for the public good, not in
the interests of private profiteers.
We won’t just restore what’s been lost. We
will invest in an Aotearoa where people and
nature flourish together.

Our plan
1. Reform conservation and wildlife
protection laws to give effect to Te
Tiriti, elevate Indigenous-led land
stewardship and ensure the conservation
management system prioritises halting
and reversing nature loss in Aotearoa.
2. Ban new mining on conservation land,
including stewardship land.
3. Expand funding for Jobs for Nature
– Mahi mō te Taiao to protect our
biodiversity and create thousands of
regional jobs.
4. Protect all remaining natural wetlands in
legislation, including coastal wetlands
and estuaries, and implement a plan to
restore at least 30% of degraded wetland
area, prioritising areas most important
for biodiversity recovery and community
resilience.
5. Fund Action for Nature, the
implementation plan for the biodiversity
strategy, and implement national
guidance to protect indigenous
biodiversity, including the protection of
taonga species.
6. Increase overall public conservation
funding, including increasing funding and
support for the Predator Free 2050 goal.

Conservation and biodiversity

Climate action:
resilience + adaptation

9

<!-- page 6 -->

An Aotearoa that values artists
The Green Party will invest in
the arts, creativity and culture
that make Aotearoa vibrant
and unique.
Our art, artists and creatives tell the stories of
our communities and help make sense of the
world around us.
This government has starved the sector
of support. Too many of our creatives are
working without the certainty of a stable
income, and many lack access to the training
and education needed to foster their skills
and talents. Steep cuts to Māori arts and
broadcasting have left them to scale down or
to fend for themselves.

Culture and creativity

Those governments have seen the arts as
a nice-to-have, rather than central to our
identity as New Zealanders. They’ve rolled
out the red carpet for big overseas studios,
sending funds offshore, while local and
Indigenous artists are left to struggle.

10

Arts, culture and creativity are vital for
creating vibrant cities and communities. Like
other community infrastructure, the arts,
culture and creative sectors need proper
support.
It is time for artists and creatives to be valued,
respected and recognised for their work.
The Green Party will fund the arts properly
and ensure artists have the long-term
sustainability, training and venues that
are necessary to build an audience and a
meaningful livelihood.
Together, we can support the people behind
the books, music, movies, shows and images
that tell our stories.

public services must care for, include and
uphold the mana of rainbow people. The
deeply connected relationships between
rainbow identities, whakapapa and whānau
must also be acknowledged and allowed to
thrive.

34

Barriers that stop people participating fully
in their communities must be removed.
Some Rainbow communities — including
takatāpui, MVPFAFF+ and Pacific LGBTQI+
communities, disabled rainbow people,
migrants, refugees, young people and
intersex people — face overlapping and
compounding barriers to a healthy life that
must be recognised and addressed.
The Green Party believes that rainbow health
care should be shaped by compassion,
evidence and aroha — not fear or political
division.
Decisions that affect communities should
be made with them, not imposed on them.
The Green Party will put people at the heart
of political decision-making, ensuring those
most impacted by policy are heard.

Our plan
1. W
 ork with the different rainbow
communities to develop appropriate
health care services and strategies, built
on cultural values and holistic models of
care and wellbeing.
2. Increase resourcing for rainbow
organisations, including dedicated
support for Māori and Pasifikaled organisations, to support the
development and delivery of services
that reflect the diverse needs, values,
and strengths of rainbow communities.
3. Resource clear pathways for timely,
free, non-discriminatory access to all
forms of gender-affirming health care
based on informed consent and selfdetermination, including reversal of the
ban on puberty blockers.
4. Promote the human rights of takatāpui,
intersex and rainbow people, amending
the Human Rights Act to clarify
that all forms of sexual orientation,
gender identity and variations in
sex characteristics, are prohibited
on grounds of discrimination, and
implement the Law Commission’s Ia
Tangata report recommendations.

Seniors

Happy, healthy and supported

The Green Party will uphold
the mana of seniors by
prioritising the support that
enables equitable and fulfilling
lives.
Seniors have cared for us and served their
communities. Many continue to do so during
retirement.
Every senior should be valued, connected
and able to live with dignity. However, the
Luxon Government has sidelined the needs
of seniors, meaning many find themselves
without the care and support they need.
Some have no one to turn to.
Guided by manaakitanga, whanaungatanga,
and led by Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we envision
communities where seniors are recognised
and celebrated as leaders and knowledge
holders, actively shaping whānau, hapū and
iwi life. Homes are warm, accessible and
designed for connection across generations,
while community spaces and marae-based
centres foster belonging, learning and
support.

5. Prohibit all non-consensual and
medically unnecessary surgeries or
medical interventions on intersex
people.

We believe those who work in aged care must
be respected and rewarded, with secure
conditions that enable them to provide
high-quality, compassionate support. Care
systems should be equitable, culturally
grounded, and responsive, ensuring Māori,
Pacific Peoples and diverse communities can
access services that reflect their values and
tikanga.

6. Reform laws and policies so rainbow
asylum seekers, refugees and migrants
can access legal gender recognition,
partnership recognition, family
reunification, and resettlement support.

The Green Party commits to a long-term,
non-partisan vision where seniors thrive
with dignity and autonomy in vibrant
intergenerational communities, ensuring that
ageing is a positive process.

Our plan
1. Launch a dedicated long-term
strategy for the needs of an ageing
population which encompasses the
holistic wellbeing of kaumātua, elder
abuse prevention, ensuring income is
equitably accessed and sufficient to live
comfortably, and the establishment of a
state-owned, not-for-profit retirement
village scheme.
2. Increase funding for community
spaces and the establishment of
facilities, programmes, education and
volunteering opportunities that are
accessible to seniors.
3. Expanding housing options by building
more papakāinga, prioritising kaumātua
on social housing waitlists, and ensuring
housing designs are suitable for their
needs — single-level and warm,
with mobility features and room for
intergenerational living.
4. Ensure support services are grounded
in cultural values, and that home and
community care workers are well
trained, supported and paid equitably
and fairly by including travel time.
5. Resource Māori, Pacific and migrant
organisations to provide kaumātua care
that is aligned with their values, cultural
practices and tikanga.

Seniors

Rainbow communities

35

<!-- page 19 -->

Championing small, local enterprise
The Green Party will back
local businesses, support
sustainable industries and
ensure small businesses have a
fair shot.

2. Commit government departments to
buying more goods and services from
Aotearoa businesses.

In the last year, we saw the highest number
of business liquidations in almost 15 years.
Local suppliers are being squeezed by the
supermarket duopoly, while factories are
closing and costing jobs. This is the story right
across our economy.

3. Foster sustainable, low-carbon jobs in
the information and communication
technology sector by expanding access
to grants and rebates for smaller sized
firms.

The Green Party will reform our economic rules
to back local businesses, even the playing field,
and support sustainable, low-carbon industries
to thrive.

Small businesses

1. Revitalise ‘Buy Kiwi Made’ and expand
country of origin labelling so it’s easier to
support local businesses.

When wealth is kept in local communities, we all
benefit. But too often, small businesses face an
economy that is stacked against them.

Successive governments have built an
economy where large international corporates
can flourish, sending immense profits offshore,
while small and local businesses fight just to
keep the lights on.

36

Our plan

4. Continue to invest in community-led
regional development with a focus
on sustainable building, regenerative
agriculture and horticulture, improving
low-carbon infrastructure, and iwi- and
hapū-led economic activity.
5. Reform competition laws to create a
fairer playing field for small businesses
and to benefit consumers. Increase the
resources and powers of regulatory
agencies to investigate anti-competitive
practice.

Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Advancing an Aotearoa that
embraces Te Tiriti

The Green Party will put Te
Tiriti o Waitangi at the heart of
a modern Aotearoa founded
on real partnership.
We envision an Aotearoa where our
governing structures uphold the
rangatiratanga of iwi and hapū, providing
dignity for all. We can achieve this by
demonstrating true partnership between
tangata whenua and the Crown as intended
by Te Tiriti.
Successive governments have consistently
breached Te Tiriti. The resulting harm, lack
of accountability and denial of Māori as equal
partners mean that the Crown has not upheld
its side of the partnership. When Te Tiriti
breaches are ongoing, apologies for past
harms are not enough.
It is our responsibility to acknowledge, take
accountability and put right the wrongdoings
committed by the Crown. These have led to
worse outcomes for Māori in too many ways.
We can’t allow government to pretend that
everyone is equal in this country when the
exact systems that were created to oppress
Māori are still operating.
The Green Party understands that He
Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti are the
foundation for an enduring constitutional
partnership. We acknowledge the need for
ongoing dialogue to build the awareness,
understanding and vision that will give life to
Te Tiriti in Aotearoa.

Our plan
1. Amend the Treaty of Waitangi Act
to recognise that Te Tiriti is the
authoritative text and that Te Tiriti works
in conjunction with He Whakaputanga o
te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni.
2. Implement genuine Te Tiriti-based
decision-making models across
government and resource iwi and hapū
to participate as partners rather than as
advisors.
3. Reform the Treaty Settlements process
by amending the settlement policy
guide for negotiators to enable fair
negotiations and just reparations
without ceding sovereignty, removing
any clauses that refer to ‘Full and
Final settlement’, ending the ‘large
natural grouping’ approach to Treaty
settlements, and validating hapū
rangatiratanga.
4. Increase resourcing for the Waitangi
Tribunal, providing them with the power
to make binding recommendations for
the return of Crown and Private land to
iwi, whānau and hapū.
5. Facilitate the return of whenua outside of
Treaty Settlements that was wrongfully
alienated from tangata whenua,
including through exploring a right-offirst-refusal process that enables the
return of private land to iwi, hapū and
whānau at point of sale.

Te Tiriti o Waitangi

Small businesses

37

<!-- page 20 -->

Opportunities for everyone
to learn and grow
The Green Party will
support student success
by overhauling tertiary
education.
We all benefit when somebody takes on
tertiary study, contributing original thought
and their skills to our communities, hapori
(community), country and the world.
Unfortunately, successive governments
have forced universities and polytechs to
make deep cuts to the courses and services
students need to succeed.
At the same time, they have normalised
student poverty, leaving students struggling
to pay the rent and eat a decent meal.
Choosing to study shouldn’t be a
commitment to years of stress and hardship.
Tertiary education should be the springboard
into a meaningful career and the expansion of
human knowledge.

Tertiary education

The Green Party will overhaul the tertiary
education sector, so our institutions are
sustainable and operate in the public good.

38

That means a tertiary education system
where it’s affordable to study, students get
the support they need to succeed, and staff
have good pay and working conditions so
that everyone can benefit from a world-class
tertiary education system.
We can ensure that we have a thriving tertiary
sector that looks after students, staff and the
communities they serve – because tertiary
education should be for everyone.

Our plan
1. Support students with a universal
student income, including at
postgraduate level, and ensure courses
that require work placements pay
students at least the living wage.
2. Overhaul funding for the tertiary sector
to ensure it delivers rigorous research,
a wide range of course options, quality
teaching, comprehensive student
services, decent pay and conditions for
staff, and full participation of disabled
students.
3. Empower polytechnics with adequate
funding and strong local control to meet
workforce and community needs, and
protect courses, campuses and staff
from cuts.

Transport

Easy, sustainable ways to get around

The Green Party will invest
in modern, sustainable, and
affordable transport options.
This will make it easier and cheaper for
people to safely get around our cities and
regions.
Aotearoa was once joined up by buses and a
reliable passenger rail system. Fast, frequent
and reliable public transport ran throughout
our cities and towns.
After our rail network was sold off for private
profit, it was returned to the people in
disarray. Successive governments have
failed to invest in our rail network or plan for
the future in our urban areas. Our cities are
now choked with cars, instead of flourishing
with people.

4. Expand free apprenticeship
programmes, reduce student loan
repayments and work towards fees-free
tertiary education and a student debt
write-off.

People have been priced out of our central
cities and now live in the outskirts, where
they are poorly served by public transport
and don’t have safe walking and biking
infrastructure. This has left so many with
no option but to rely on cars to get around,
adding to congestion and making people
vulnerable to oil price shocks.

5. Ensure all tertiary institutes uphold Te
Tiriti o Waitangi and deliver equitable
outcomes for ākonga Māori (Māori
students). Expand the Māori and
Pasifika Trades Training programme,
and fully resource Whare Wānanga to
increase opportunities for kaupapa
Māori education.

The Green Party will invest in transport for
the future so we all have real options to get
around our communities, wherever we live.
We’ll ease congestion with rapid buses and
surface light rail in our biggest cities. We
will fund councils to build linked-up bike
networks, and invest in rail to move people
and freight.

6. Return to default student union
membership and develop a governance
model for tertiary organisations in
which staff, students, communities and
tangata whenua govern together.

Giving people the freedom to take public
transport or bike instead of being forced into
cars will provide them immediate relief where
it counts — their wallets.

Our plan
1. Transform public transport networks,
including building mass rapid transit in
Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch,
and providing comprehensive bus lanes
in all cities.
2. Invest in nationwide rapid rail for
passengers and freight to connect
regions and major cities and contribute
to economic development and
decarbonisation.
3. Introduce targeted subsidies for e-cargo
bikes. Introduce e-bike sharing schemes
in community hubs, to allow more
families to save on transport costs.
4. Fund affordable, reliable, interregional
rural bus services, and on-demand
public transport, including by-Māori forMāori public transport to serve kōhanga
reo and rural schools.
5. Extend Community Connect to provide
free fares for students and apprentices,
community service card holders,
everyone under 18, and all Total Mobility
card holders.
6. Enable the provision of transport
services publicly instead of for profit
by replacing the Public Transport
Operating Model.
7. Create safe walking and biking routes to
all community hubs including schools
through building more bike lanes and
safe crossings, and lowering speed
limits near schools.
8. Implement a phase-out date for the
import of fossil-fuel powered vehicles,
build more EV (electric vehicle) charging
stations, remove regulatory barriers
to EV car-sharing and re-introduce
incentives for EV uptake.

Transport

Tertiary education

39

<!-- page 21 -->

Keeping whānau and communities safe
The Green Party will make sure
everyone can live a life free from
violence and heal from trauma.
Our homes, whānau and communities should
be places of aroha, care and safety — free from
fear and harm.
Aotearoa has among the highest rates of
intimate partner violence, sexual violence
and child abuse. This disproportionately
harms people in vulnerable professions and
communities, and can have long-lasting
impacts that are passed down through families.
The current Government has stalled progress
on work initiated by the Green Party to prevent
violence from happening. They have failed to
deliver action, instead cutting funding to critical
community-led services.

Violence prevention

The Green Party will invest in stopping violence
before it starts. Our approach will be safe,
accessible and integrated, building on people’s
strength and with Te Tiriti o Waitangi at its
heart. We will mobilise our communities to
help and ensure our workforce is skilled and
culturally competent.

40

New Zealanders deserve a government who are
committed to ending violence in Aotearoa. We
will invest in tailored specialist and whānaucentred services for victims and survivors
focused on prevention, healing, recovery
and restoration. This includes services to
support those who have used violence to take
accountability and change their behaviour.
The Green Party vision is an Aotearoa where
everyone feels safe and supported.

Our plan
1. Fund the implementation of the action
plan for Te Aorerekura: National
Strategy to Eliminate Family Violence
and Sexual Violence, centred on Te
Tiriti.
2. Resource kaupapa Māori solutions
and community-led solutions to family
and sexual violence, that have been
developed by disproportionately
impacted groups, including women,
Pasifika, rainbow, and disabled
communities.
3. Prioritise violence responses and
prevention by improving workforce and
broader public understanding of the
drivers and signs of violence, and how
to respond in ways that enhance safety
and healing.
4. Amend the Crimes Act to criminalise
coercive control, amend the definition
of consent, and preclude a defence of
reluctant consent to affirm that consent
must be free and voluntary, and can be
withdrawn at any time while ensuring
these changes cause no further harm.
5. Restore relationship and sexuality
teaching guidelines — including
education on healthy relationships,
diverse identities and sexualities, and
affirmative consent — in all schools.
6. Increase funding for counselling and
mental health support for victims,
whānau, witnesses, defendants and
legal professionals engaging in the
justice system.

Welfare of animals
Caring for all animals
that call Aotearoa home

The Green Party will keep
animals safe from cruelty and
suffering.
Animals should live a happy, comfortable life
free from suffering.
Unfortunately, the Luxon Government has let
big industry players write our animal welfare
laws, putting corporate greed ahead of the
wellbeing of animals.
Thousands of farmed animals are suffering
unnecessarily because the standards that
are meant to protect their safety aren’t being
upheld. Cruel and harmful practices are
allowed to continue.
The Green Party will protect animals from
practices that put profit ahead of their
welfare. We have been the parliamentary
champion for animal welfare for decades.
In recent years, we have fought for and
protected the ban on live exports at sea and
won the end to greyhound racing. We have
been the leading parliamentary voice against
mud farming, cruel imports and the caging of
mother pigs.
The Green Party will transform our animal
welfare protections to make Aotearoa a place
where all animals are treated with care and
respect.
We will prioritise ethical treatment so that
all animals can live a good life no matter
where they live — on farms, in our homes or
in the wild.

Our plan
1. Create a new Commissioner for Animals
to independently monitor and advocate
for the rights of animals, and an
independent ministry.
2. Resource the National Animal Welfare
Advisory Committee to ensure all animal
welfare codes genuinely comply with
the Animal Welfare Act, and introduce
stronger codes for farmed animals.
3. Phase out harmful activities including
debeaking of hens, intensive winter
grazing, factory farming, octopus
farming, farrowing crates and rodeo.
4. Require that imported products
meet the animal welfare standards of
Aotearoa, including for cosmetics.
5. Introduce consistent, clear
and enforceable standards for
manufacturing claims about animal
welfare and ingredients (such as ‘free
range’, ‘cruelty free’ and ‘vegan’).
6. Retain the ban on live exports of farmed
animals by sea and extend the ban to
include live exports of farmed animals
by air and wild-caught animals such as
endangered tuna longfin eels.

Welfare of animals

Violence prevention

41

<!-- page 22 -->

Employment protections and
decent pay for all workers
The Green Party will protect
rights, improve conditions
and make things fairer for
workers.
Work should provide dignity, security and
a fair share in the prosperity we create
together. Strong employment rights, decent
pay and collective voice are essential for a
thriving economy and a healthy democracy.
Workers should be valued for their
contribution, protected from exploitation and
supported to live well — not just survive.

Workforce rights

Right now, too many people are locked
into insecure, low-paid or unsafe work.
Employers hold the balance of power
and unemployment is used to suppress
workers’ fair expectations for better pay and
conditions.

42

The current Government has launched
a sustained attack on workers’ rights
— removing pay equity and fair pay
agreements, cutting health and safety
protections, and normalising insecurity.
Meanwhile, industries producing important
goods for Aotearoa are forced to close when
international corporations aren’t happy with
their bottom line.
The Green Party will implement a workforce
system built on fairness, democracy and
care, restoring the balance between workers
and employers. This means standing up
for pay equity, safe workplaces and secure
employment.
We will undo this Government’s attacks on
workers and build strong, future-focused
employment protections. Our plan will
support a flourishing economy that works
for everyone — through the transition to a
sustainable zero carbon economy.

Our plan
1. Strengthen worker bargaining power
by changing employment law to default
union membership. This means people
automatically join a union when they
start a new job, but can opt out later.
Expand the right to strike, including for
breaches of collective agreements and
political and solidarity reasons.
2. Strengthen employment law to protect
all workers’ free time with a right to
disconnect. Ensure protection from
unwanted contact or surveillance out of
working hours.
3. Explore legislating to put workers’
representatives on boards of publicly
listed companies.
4. Guarantee annual minimum wage
increases that at least keep up with
inflation. Pay all publicly funded roles a
living wage. Work towards matching the
minimum wage to the living wage.
5. Increase paid parental leave to 15
months for the primary caregiver,
with additional ring-fenced leave
for partners, while also increasing
payments.
6. Protect platform and gig-economy
workers by strengthening the test for
whether a worker is a contractor.
7. Close the gender and ethnic pay gaps
by undoing the Government’s changes
to the pay equity regime and resuming
claims, pay transparency measures, and
comprehensive pay gap reporting.

Zero waste

Building a sustainable circular economy

The Green Party will take
action to reduce waste and
protect the environment from
pollution.
In a truly sustainable system, nature is
protected rather than treated as a dumping
ground. We can build a circular economy
where waste is designed out and resources
are valued and reused.
Under the current Government, progress
towards our zero-waste future has stalled.
Action on plastic pollution has ground to a
halt, and funding for solutions has dried up.
Corporations continue to make products that
won’t last or can’t be repaired, filling up our
landfills. Communities are left to deal with the
pollution and impacts.
The Green Party has shown what’s possible.
In government, we banned single-use plastic
bags and reduced food waste going to
landfill. We increased the waste levy for the
first time in over a decade and introduced
mandatory product stewardship schemes.
We also started work on a container return
scheme.
We will build on this legacy by holding
corporations accountable for the waste they
create. This means both reducing waste, and
requiring the recovery, recycling, reuse and
redistribution of materials.
By supporting communities to lead local
solutions, we will accelerate the transition
to a sustainable and circular economy that
allows people and nature to thrive.

Our plan
1. Establish strong product policy
measures, including mandatory
product stewardship, a beverage
container return scheme, phaseouts of problematic products and
comprehensive right-to-repair.
2. Direct revenue from the waste disposal
levy into waste minimisation initiatives
and stop diverting the local government
portion to other purposes. Increase the
levy to match international best practice
and apply a consistent rate across all
landfill classes.
3. Introduce a moratorium on wasteto-energy plants and explore energy
generation from biogas associated with
animal and plant wastes.
4. Build on proposed reforms of the Waste
Minimisation Act to implement timely,
binding, measurable and ambitious
waste reduction targets. Ensure
legislation gives effect to Te Tiriti o
Waitangi. Introduce comprehensive
duty-of-care systems for the waste and
resource recovery sector covering all
waste streams, including hazardous
waste.
5. Make greater use of discarded soil.
Divert soil from landfills, where safe and
appropriate to do so.
6. Prioritise local, mana whenua and
community-driven solutions to
resource recovery, implementation of
national zero-waste strategies, and
organic waste reduction, diversion and
processing.

Zero waste

Workforce rights

43

<!-- page 23 -->

FOR ALL
OF US.

Authorised by Miriam Ross, greens.org.nz

# Green Party Māori Manifesto 2026 — Taiao, Tāngata, Tāhua, Rangatiratanga: Kei ō tātou ringa

<!-- page 1 -->

Authorised by Miriam Ross, greens.org.nz

<!-- page 2 -->

TAIAO
TĀNGATA
TĀHUA
RANGATIRATANGA

KEI Ō TĀTOU RINGA.
