# Government in the Economy Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/government_in_the_economy_policy#government_in_the_economy_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64724/attachments/original/1778624605/Policy-Greens_Government_Economy_Policy_2024-2026.pdf)

## Summary

This policy outlines the role of the Government in transforming the economy. In Government, the Green Party will tackle inequality through a fairer tax system, providing everyone with public services and infrastructure to meet their material, social, and cultural needs. We will limit our use of resources to live within planetary boundaries and urgently address the climate crisis. We will support Māori understandings and expectations of economic justice. We will retain and expand public investment in direct service provision and assets.

OUR VISION

> An economy that equitably serves both present and future generations and cares for the natural world.

## Values and Principles

Policy decisions must be consistent with the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Economic activity must support equity and self-determination for Māori while protecting all taonga.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Our economy must urgently adjust to operate within environmental limits to ensure the natural world can continue to support human life.

##### Social Responsibility:

Economic benefits and burdens must be fairly distributed to enable all New Zealanders to participate fully in society and have their collective material needs met.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

The economy must be democratically managed. Communities and tangata whenua must have meaningful influence over decisions about economic activities that affect them.

##### Non-Violence:

Economic activity must not exploit or oppress peoples or environments. Any activity that negatively affects communities or environments must be minimised and mitigated.

##### Fiscal and economic transparency:

Economic reporting must be comprehensive, clear, reliable, and timely.

##### Creativity:

Creativity and innovation help us to reduce resource use and support collective wellbeing.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“We want to transform our economy, replacing consumerism, consumption and growth with a non-polluting, regenerative economy that enables all people to thrive within nature’s bounty.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Enabling the economy to respond urgently to the climate crisis and work within ecological limits, including by incorporating the true cost of environmental damage into the cost of doing business in Aotearoa New Zealand. (2.4.2)
- Substantially increasing government revenue and expenditure as a proportion of GDP to fully fund high-quality and universal health, education, accessibility, transport and other social services, and to ensure everyone has access to adequate energy, housing and food. (3.1.2)
- Enabling greater government borrowing for investing in infrastructure. (4.2.2.1)

- Expanding the progressive tax system to equitably tax wealth and all forms of income, such as through capital gains, land, land value, wealth, and inheritance taxes. (3.3.3)
- Developing Tiriti-based Public-Commons Partnerships that provide for collective management of, and equitable access to, shared resources. (1.2.2)
- Broadening the Reserve Bank’s focus to ensure that it supports the economy and full employment while controlling inflation. (4.2.1)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64724/attachments/original/1778624605/Policy-Greens_Government_Economy_Policy_2024-2026.pdf)

## Connected Policies

The big-picture approach of this policy is designed to enable more specific policy outcomes such as:

- Ensuring that the private sector can provide products and services that support wellbeing within environmental limits: [Business Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/sustainable_business_policy); [Climate Change Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy); [Housing and Sustainable Communities Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy)
- Supporting resilient local economies: [Community and the Economy Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/community_and_the_economy_policy)
- Ensuring that everyone in Aotearoa New Zealand has a sufficient income to meet their needs and participate fully in society: [Livelihoods Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/household_livelihoods_policy); [Workforce Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy)
- Growing a circular economy through business tax incentives, support for local authority waste reduction initiatives and other measures: [Waste and Hazardous Substances Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/waste_and_hazardous_substances_policy)
- Ensuring that everyone has access to high-quality, universal public services such as education, healthcare, accessibility assistance and public transport: [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/education_policy), [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy), [Transport](https://www.greens.org.nz/transport_policy), [Livelihoods](https://www.greens.org.nz/household_livelihoods_policy) and [Disability](https://www.greens.org.nz/disability_policy) Policies

- Ensuring that everyone has access to adequate food, energy, and housing: [Food](https://www.greens.org.nz/food_policy), [Energy](https://www.greens.org.nz/energy_policy), and [Housing and Sustainable Communities](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy) Policies
- Ensuring that economic decision-making is responsive and evidence-based through independent evaluation, to manage the complexity and interconnectedness of the economy with almost every aspect of our lives: [Governance Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/democracy_and_constitutional_transformation_policy)
- Ensuring that trade and investment frameworks specifically recognise ecological limits and the priority to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions: [Global Affairs Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/global_affairs_policy); [Trade and Foreign Investment Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/trade_and_foreign_investment_policy)

Specific economic sectors are also considered in separate policies, including [Energy](https://www.greens.org.nz/energy_policy), [Agriculture](https://www.greens.org.nz/agriculture_and_rural_affairs_policy), [Tourism](https://www.greens.org.nz/tourism_policy), [Forestry](https://www.greens.org.nz/forestry_policy), and [Research, Science and Technology](https://www.greens.org.nz/research_science_and_technology_policy) Policies.

# Housing and Sustainable Communities Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy#housing_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64752/attachments/original/1781650001/Policy-Greens_Housing_and_Sustainable_Communities_Policy_2022-2026.pdf?1781650001)

## Summary

The Green Party will ensure people’s right to healthy, secure housing. We will focus on: launching a massive public housing project that is funded, managed and run by the government; providing for a substantial increase in Māori housing and the removal of barriers to Māori housing; making housing accessibility and safety for disabled people a high priority; reducing building-related greenhouse gas emissions; and creating frameworks to ensure regenerative urban development that connects people within their communities.

OUR VISION

> Accessible, healthy, secure and sustainable housing for all in thriving communities.

## Values and Principles

This housing policy must be consistent with the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Article 2 of Te Tiriti o Waitangi guarantees tangata whenua tino rangatiratanga over their taonga, which includes their whenua. Honouring this guarantee is fundamental to enabling housing developments, including papakāinga. Funding should be prioritised for Māori housing developments, with ownership and decision-making by Māori. Mātauranga Māori principles of design for housing and communities should be broadly applied across the whole housing sector to build adequate housing for all.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Our communities must be life-sustaining. They should be designed, built or renovated using principles, materials and processes that are regenerative and minimise negative environmental impacts.

##### Social Responsibility:

People should have access to healthy, affordable and secure homes that support wellbeing and enable connected, inclusive communities. Housing needs to be designed as universally accessible so that all groups in the community have equitable access to appropriate and affordable housing.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

Communities should be actively involved in decisions that affect the places they live. Decision making should particularly consider the interests of those who have been marginalised, and actively ensure their inclusion in community engagement processes.

##### Non-Violence:

Vested private interests that seek to maintain control of housing should be mitigated by the government through legislation and engagement to neutralise the power imbalance. No one should be forced to move out of their home without a suitable alternative being provided.

##### Decommodification:

Housing should be seen as a fundamental human need and right, not something that is traded for capital gains and profits that serve to perpetuate inequality. Basically, houses should be homes.

##### Housing security:

People should be able to live in their home or community for as long as they wish, regardless of ownership. Having generations of family/whānau living together contributes to stable and healthy communities.

##### Housing for disabled people:

Disabled people have the right to live in accessible housing both wherever and with whomever they choose to live with.

## Strategic Priorities

“Healthy homes within thriving neighbourhoods will be available to everyone. People will be part of caring communities with a strong heritage fabric and easy access to the natural environment.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Sufficiently resourcing papakāinga and other Māori-led housing solutions and Māori community housing providers (1.2.1)
- Establishing a right to housing in legislation that requires the State to ensure all New Zealanders are adequately housed in safe, healthy, accessible, affordable housing. (2.1.1)
- Establishing a Ministry for Green Works to ensure supply of suitable housing for all New Zealanders (...) (3.4.1)

- Establishing representative housing committees in all local communities that reflect both homeowners and renters (4.6.2)
- Creating regulatory structures, including affordable housing requirements, that require developers to provide for equitable developments. (4.3.2)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64752/attachments/original/1781650001/Policy-Greens_Housing_and_Sustainable_Communities_Policy_2022-2026.pdf?1781650001)

## Connected Policies

To address the housing crisis, alongside the actions below the [Government in the Economy](https://www.greens.org.nz/government_in_the_economy_policy) must incentivise productive [Business](https://www.greens.org.nz/business_policy) investment and savings to support [Livelihoods](https://www.greens.org.nz/livelihoods_policy), and disincentivise property speculation. Sustainable development is an important part of protecting [Biodiversity and Environmental Regeneration](https://www.greens.org.nz/biodiversity_environmental_regeneration_policy), including restoring urban [Freshwater](https://www.greens.org.nz/freshwater_policy) ecosystems. Key to sustainable development are minimising suburban sprawl in favour of regenerative [Land Use and Soils](https://www.greens.org.nz/land_use_and_soils_policy), reducing the impacts of [Climate Change](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy), minimising [Energy](https://www.greens.org.nz/energy_policy) use, enabling and prioritising low-carbon [Transport](https://www.greens.org.nz/transport_policy), and focusing on [Community in the Economy](https://www.greens.org.nz/community_and_the_economy_policy). See our [Kaupapa Māori Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/kaupapa_maori) for pathways for returning Māori ancestral lands to Māori ownership.

# Human Rights Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/human_rights_policy#human_rights_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64766/attachments/original/1781650300/Policy-Greens_Human_Rights_Policy_2024-2026.pdf?1781650300)

## Summary

The Green Party is committed to ensuring that everyone’s human rights are upheld. We will honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi by strengthening the rights of Tāngata Whenua through a te ao Māori lens. We will safeguard the rights of future generations. We will extend our laws to cover more human rights, sign up to more international treaties, and give the courts and human rights institutions more power to uphold human rights.

OUR VISION

> Everyone’s rights are safeguarded and actively upheld so that everyone can participate equitably.

## Values and Principles

Decisions relating to human rights must uphold the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Tino rangatiratanga must be fundamental to the human rights framework of Aotearoa New Zealand and be upheld at all levels.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Equitable access to a healthy environment is a fundamental human right and essential to the rights of future generations.

##### Social Responsibility:

Everyone has a right to an adequate standard of living, and to take part in social, economic and cultural activities.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

Everyone must be empowered to exercise their democratic rights. Everyone has a right to live free from discrimination and groups that currently face structural marginalisation have a right to equity.

##### Non-Violence:

Diversity must be not only celebrated, but actively protected. Everyone must be able to live free from discrimination, fear, violence and abuse.

##### International Cooperation:

Aotearoa New Zealand must use our resources and voice to support the human rights of other people and nations.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“As a Party we strive to create a more connected, compassionate and equitable Aotearoa, free from structural biases that discriminate against groups and individuals.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Establishing a human rights framework that enables human rights issues to be resolved appropriately and implements the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), informed by Tikanga Māori, Matike Mai, Mātauranga Māori, He Whakaputanga, and Te Tiriti o Waitangi. (1.1.3)
- Developing enduring legal frameworks that explicitly protects the rights of future generations. (2.1.3)
- Implementing the recommendations of the Royal Commission on the Christchurch Mosque Attacks regarding hate speech and hate crimes, and extending hate speech laws to cover religious or ethical belief, disability, gender (including gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation and sex characteristics. (3.1.1)

- Extending the prohibited grounds of discrimination in the Human Rights Act to cover caste, union activity, appearance, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, sex characteristics, and all sexual orientations, and reviewing the exceptions to the prohibitions on discrimination to ensure they do not harm or exclude marginalised groups. (3.1.2)
- Extending the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act to cover other human rights recognised in international human rights instruments, such as social, economic and cultural rights, the right to privacy, the right to self-determination and children’s rights, and ensuring that our laws and practices are consistent with them. (3.3.3)
- Making the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act supreme law and entrenching it. (3.4.3)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64766/attachments/original/1781650300/Policy-Greens_Human_Rights_Policy_2024-2026.pdf?1781650300)

## Connected Policies

All Green Party policies apply the concept of human rights, including upholding the rights of tangata whenua under [Te Tiriti o Waitangi](https://www.greens.org.nz/te_tiriti_policy). Our [Workforce Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy) upholds the rights of workers. Our [Immigration Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/immigration_policy) upholds the rights of refugees and migrants. Our [Justice Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/justice_policy) upholds the right to justice and the rights of detainees. Our policy treats access to [Housing](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy) and [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy) as human rights. Our [Governance Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/governance_policy) creates robust and effective legal rights for the natural world. Our [Disability Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/disability_policy) upholds the rights of disabled people. Other policies uphold the rights of [Children](https://www.greens.org.nz/children_policy), [Women](https://www.greens.org.nz/womens_policy), the [Rainbow](https://www.greens.org.nz/rainbow) community and [Tagata Moana](https://www.greens.org.nz/tagata_moana_policy).

# Immigration Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/immigration_policy#immigration_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64780/attachments/original/1778624607/Policy-Greens_Immigration_Policy_2017-2026.pdf)

## Summary

For those who would like to come to live in Aotearoa New Zealand, the Green Party will ensure that the process of selecting immigrants is fair, reasonable and flexible, and that immigrants are treated with dignity and respect, including, for example, through family reunification and fair employment conditions. The Green Party believes that Aotearoa New Zealand should remain firm in our commitment and humanitarian responsibilities towards international refugees and asylum seekers.

OUR VISION

> A progressive immigration system that is humane, fair, practical, sustainable, and sensitive to the requirements and concerns of all migrants as well as tangata whenua and tangata Tiriti.

## Values and Principles

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

The right for non-Māori to live in Aotearoa New Zealand derives from Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Māori, as tangata whenua, should have a partnership role in determining Aotearoa New Zealand's immigration policies.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Immigration policy should consider the environmental impacts of population changes and support climate goals.

##### Social Responsibility:

All immigration applicants, migrants, asylum seekers and refugees, should be treated with dignity, compassion and respect in accordance with international conventions on human rights.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

Immigration processes should be open, accountable and responsive. Local communities should be involved in policy decision-making and implementation.

##### Non-Violence:

All migrants and refugees should be welcomed and included in Aotearoa New Zealand society, such that they feel a sense of belonging. Tolerance, acceptance and understanding is important in a diverse and multicultural society.

##### Responsibility:

Aotearoa New Zealand should act as a responsible member of the international community. Aotearoa New Zealand is a Pacific nation with a Pacific history and its immigration policies and practices should reflect that.

##### Distributed benefits:

The positive contributions that migrants make to the social, cultural and economic life of Aotearoa New Zealand should be shared across all regions, not just in the main centres.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“As a Party we strive to create a more connected, compassionate and equal Aotearoa, free from structural biases that discriminate against groups and individuals.
“Comprehensive support for communities and individuals affected (...) by the impacts of climate change within New Zealand and the Pacific will be well established.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Actively support Māori aspirations for a Tiriti-based immigration system (...). (1.1)
- Advocate for a Pacific Passport to allow for free movement between the islands and Aotearoa. (2.1.1)
- Make specific provision in immigration legislation for people displaced by climate change, based on need. (2.1.2)

- Ensure that immigration policies do not discriminate based on applicants' countries of origin, ethnicities, cultures, age, gender, sexual orientation, and all other prohibited grounds of discrimination. (3.1)
- Increase our refugee quota and the resources required to provide adequate refugee services. (4.1.2)
- Require employers to pay temporary workers no less than local workers, and to provide them with the same working conditions as local workers. (6.9.1)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64780/attachments/original/1778624607/Policy-Greens_Immigration_Policy_2017-2026.pdf)

## Connected Policies

Refugees are part of our Pacific-oriented and [Human Rights](https://www.greens.org.nz/human_rights_policy)-based approach to [Global Affairs](https://www.greens.org.nz/global_affairs_policy) and [Climate Change](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy). Migrant workers are part of our [Workforce](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy) and contribute to [Business](https://www.greens.org.nz/business_policy) success. Migrants, including international students, must be well-supported in [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/education_policy) and by other public services, such as [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy) and public [Housing](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy).

# Justice Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/justice_policy#justice_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64794/attachments/original/1781652265/Policy-Greens_Justice_Policy_2025-2026.pdf?1781652265)

## Summary

The Green Party envisages a justice system based on Te Tiriti o Waitangi, tikanga Māori and te ao Māori values. We will prioritise restorative justice, rehabilitation, and community responses to offending. We will focus on prevention, early intervention, and addressing underlying issues such as mental health. We will tackle bias, discrimination and inequalities in the justice system, while removing barriers to access to justice and strengthening accountability to ensure that it upholds everyone’s rights.

OUR VISION

> The justice system heals and protects people and communities equitably.

## Values and Principles

Decisions relating to the justice system must uphold the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Tikanga Māori is the first law of Aotearoa. The justice system should uphold tino rangatiratanga and ensure equity for Māori.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Environmental justice is an integral part of justice. The legal system should protect nature now and in the future.

##### Social Responsibility:

Everyone is entitled to equitable access to justice, to a fair hearing, and to be treated with respect in the justice system. Everyone deserves an opportunity to atone for past wrongs and to reintegrate into society.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

The rule of law and judicial independence are fundamental to achieving justice. Transparency is necessary to ensure that justice is both done and seen to be done.

##### Non-Violence:

The justice system should engage all participants with compassion, ensure support is available, and seek to be transformative and restorative rather than punitive.

##### International Obligations:

Honouring international obligations and institutions is necessary to ensure justice and peace, both internationally and in Aotearoa New Zealand.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“As a Party we strive to create a more connected, compassionate, and equal Aotearoa, free from structural biases that discriminate against groups and individuals.“
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Establishing a Mana Ōrite (equal power) governance model under which Māori and Crown agencies share in justice sector decision-making. (1.1.2)
- Investing in a Tiriti-based primary prevention and early intervention model. (1.2.1)
- Funding restorative and transformative justice initiatives, including through Rangatahi and Matariki Courts. (1.3.1)
- Expanding legal aid eligibility to cover all people who need it, increasing payment rates, and providing it as grants. (2.1.3)

- Enabling judicial discretion in sentencing, including by abolishing mandatory minimum sentences, life sentences, preventive detention, limits on sentence discounts, and limits on when home detention can be imposed instead of imprisonment. (3.6.2)
- Increasing funding for counselling and mental health support for victims, whānau, witnesses, defendants, and legal professionals engaging in the justice system. (3.13.1)
- Replacing youth justice residences and boot camps with whānau and community-based rehabilitation services for young people. (3.14.1)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64794/attachments/original/1781652265/Policy-Greens_Justice_Policy_2025-2026.pdf?1781652265)

## Connected Policies

The justice system must uphold [Human Rights](https://www.greens.org.nz/human_rights_policy) and [Te Tiriti o Waitangi](https://www.greens.org.nz/te_tiriti_policy). Prisoner voting and constitutional issues are addressed in the [Governance Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/governance_policy), while the [Global Affairs Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/global_affairs_policy) covers international law. Crime and justice issues are connected to social and economic inequalities that are addressed in policies such as [Livelihoods](https://www.greens.org.nz/household_livelihoods_policy), [Housing and Sustainable Communities](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy), and [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/education_policy). Failure to provide timely and sufficient [Disability](https://www.greens.org.nz/disability_policy) and mental [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy) support contributes to the overrepresentation of disabled people, including neurodivergent people and people with mental health conditions, in the justice system. Drug laws are addressed in the [Drug Law Reform Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/drug_policy). Pay equity and workers’ rights are covered in the [Workforce Policy](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy) and are relevant to workers in the justice sector.

# Land Use and Soils Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/land_use_and_soils_policy#land_use_and_soils_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64822/attachments/original/1778624608/Policy-Greens_Land_Use_and_Soils_Policy_2022-2025.pdf)

## Summary

The Green Party will improve the ways we use and care for land, for the sake of current and future generations, other species, and ecosystem health. We will ensure that land use and land cover are managed in accordance with Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Protecting soils and minimising the impacts of mining will be priorities.

OUR VISION

> Land and soil ecosystems are protected and regenerated for present and future generations, to nurture our wellbeing and livelihoods, and provide food, medicine, and spiritual fulfilment.

## Values and Principles

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

We affirm tino rangatiratanga of iwi, hapū and whānau as kaitiaki of this whenua. The perspectives, approaches, needs, and aspirations of tangata whenua are embedded in the philosophy and approach to land and soil management.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

We must respect land and soil as part of the ecosystems we rely on. Soil ecosystems have intrinsic value, and humanity needs to steward the natural world by understanding and working within the carrying capacity of the land.

##### Social Responsibility:

The need for equity in the sustainable use of land and soil resources is acknowledged.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

Good governance (i.e., the processes by which institutions and other parties make and implement decisions in order to manage resources efficiently and ensure human rights), and strong institutions should underpin land and soil management.

##### Non-Violence:

Conflict resolution over land and soil management should ensure no violence is felt by te taiao, the creatures that call it home, and always honour Te Tiriti.

##### The mauri of land:

its cultural, spiritual, historical, conservation and ecological aspects - are prioritised. At the same time, agricultural land is valued for its ability to produce healthy food, fibre and wood and is regenerated and managed sustainably to ensure that its productive potential is protected and enhanced.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“All native species and their habitats will be thriving or on a path to recovery in terrestrial, freshwater and marine environments.
Our laws and practices will respect the biological integrity of all life, while prioritising the health of indigenous species and ecosystems.
The customary and decision making roles of whānau, hapū and iwi will be integral to decisions about resource use.
Decision-making about resource use will provide for community participation and environmental justice.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Upholding the right of tangata whenua to exercise customary practices regarding soil sovereignty and māra kai on their land. (1.1.2)
- Using both mātauranga Māori and Western science in research and the development of land and soil policies and practices. (2.1.3)
- Encouraging and resourcing landowners and communities to set marginal and erosion-prone lands aside for permanent revegetation. (1.5.1)

- Encouraging and supporting the use of soil conservation and earthworks best practice, including mechanical and biological control techniques (2.2.3)
- Ensure that the regulatory framework for mining avoids and mitigates harms (3.1)
- End the extraction of coal, oil, and gas, consistent with the urgency and necessity of limiting global heating to 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels (3.5)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64822/attachments/original/1778624608/Policy-Greens_Land_Use_and_Soils_Policy_2022-2025.pdf)

## Connected Policies

This policy discusses land use and soils within the context of [Biodiversity and Environmental Regeneration](https://www.greens.org.nz/biodiversity_environmental_regeneration_policy), alongside our [Freshwater](https://www.greens.org.nz/freshwater_policy) and [Marine](https://www.greens.org.nz/marine_policy) Policies.  Land health is impacted by human activity, including [Agriculture](https://www.greens.org.nz/agriculture_and_rural_affairs_policy), [Forestry](https://www.greens.org.nz/forestry_policy), [Housing and Sustainable Communities](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy), [Waste and Hazardous Substances](https://www.greens.org.nz/waste_and_hazardous_substances_policy), and [Climate Change](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy). Resource extraction from land can be minimised through resource and [Waste](https://www.greens.org.nz/waste_and_hazardous_substances_policy) management, including circular economy practices.

For our response to colonial land dispossession, please see our [Kaupapa Māori](https://www.greens.org.nz/kaupapa_maori) and [Te Tiriti o Waitangi](https://www.greens.org.nz/te_tiriti_policy) Policies.

# Livelihoods Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/livelihoods_policy#livelihoods_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64836/attachments/original/1778624609/Policy-Greens_Livelihoods_Policy_2025.pdf)

## Summary

The Green Party will take a Tiriti-based approach to financial and material security. We will ensure that the income support system is sufficient, accessible, and dignifying, and recognises unpaid labour. We will support low-income households to minimise debt, including regulating lenders. We will ensure that everyone has access to the services and resources they need to meet their basic needs.

OUR VISION

> Everyone has enough income and resources to live a fulfilling life with dignity and participate fully in society.

## Values and Principles

Income support and other related policy decisions must be consistent with the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Hapū and iwi Māori have the right to self-determination of their livelihoods.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

We can choose to have a thriving society, where everyone has enough, that works in harmony with the natural world.

##### Social Responsibility:

We have a responsibility to equitably support all those who live on this land to flourish.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

Decisions must be made through appropriate engagement with experts and those impacted by the decision, to find effective pathways forward.

##### Non-Violence:

Everyone has the right to livelihoods that are free from institutionalised violence, coercion and discrimination.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“Poverty will be eliminated, everyone will have enough income and wealth will be held more equally.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Increasing main benefit levels to a liveable income and ensuring supplementary benefits are sufficient. (1.2.1)
- Ensure that welfare service delivery is proactive, mana-enhancing, accessible, and inclusive of a diverse range of people’s needs (1.3)
- Establishing a legal right to a minimum income and guaranteeing this income. (1.4.3)

- Pass legislation that prevents exploitative lending and debt collection, relating to both currency and goods. (2.2)
- Resourcing underfunded basic services that support well-being, including preventative and/or early intervention services. (3.1.1)
- Legislating clear rights, rooted in Te Tiriti o Waitangi, for basic resources, and legislating the responsibilities of the Crown to provide them. (3.2.3)

Full Policy Link

## Connected Policies

As well as income support, the role of the [Government in the Economy](https://www.greens.org.nz/government_in_the_economy_policy) includes taxation and redistribution of wealth. Livelihoods are also affected by policy areas such as [Workforce](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy), [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/tertiary_education_policy), [Housing](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy), and [Climate Change](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy). Some areas experience more livelihood challenges with cascading impacts (see our [Community and the Economy](https://www.greens.org.nz/community_and_the_economy_policy), [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy) and [Justice](https://www.greens.org.nz/justice_policy) Policy, for example), as do different sectors (e.g. [Agriculture](https://www.greens.org.nz/agriculture_and_rural_affairs_policy) and [Arts](https://www.greens.org.nz/arts_culture_and_heritage_policy)).

# Climate Action: Emissions Reduction

### **Bold action and solutions that hold polluters to account**

**The Green Party will drive meaningful action, cutting climate pollution and making big polluters pay.**

We will ensure that polluting corporations pay for Aotearoa to electrify our economy. By rapidly phasing out fossil fuels, we can ease cost of living pressures and decrease our vulnerability to global price shocks.

Under the leadership of a Green Minister for Climate Change, emissions began to drop. But now, the current Government is deliberately making choices to take us off that track. In Aotearoa, progress towards our domestic climate targets is at risk. Our international reputation has been tarnished due to this Government’s decisions to weaken our climate targets and exempt our biggest polluters from paying for their greenhouse gas emissions, undermining international agreements we have signed up to.

Decades of climate inaction shows that a hands-off government will fail to decarbonise our economy and secure the future everyone deserves. The market will not respond to the climate crisis at the scale or pace we need, and won’t give fair outcomes for those most affected.

We need political leadership that stops emissions at source, makes polluters pay, and focuses all government institutions on limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees.

The Green Party will implement climate solutions that tackle the root causes and honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi. We will remove economic incentives that encourage and enable climate pollution.

### **Our plan**

1. Strengthen the Zero Carbon Act by requiring the government Budget process to be consistent with limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees, gross emissions reduction targets and international commitments.
2. Empower the Climate Change Commission to directly set unit supply in the Emissions Trading Scheme, in line with emissions budgets. Align the government Budget process with the National Adaptation Plan and Emissions Reduction Plans.
3. Introduce a price on agricultural emissions to ensure methane reduction targets are met, with financial and technical support for on-farm emissions reduction.
4. Reform the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) to restore credibility to the market by phasing out the free allocation of units, removing forestry offsetting so the system functions as a genuine ‘cap-and-trade’ system, and redirecting funding from the reformed ETS to an improved Government Investment in Decarbonising Industry Fund.
5. Ensure Aotearoa meets our Paris Agreement commitments through strong domestic action and, if necessary, environmentally and socially responsible initiatives overseas.
6. Improve public transparency on the costs of inaction by including the fiscal impact of the Nationally Determined Contribution obligation in the financial statements.

# Children

### Thriving tamariki and rangatahi.

**The Green Party will work to build a system that puts tamariki, rangatahi and whānau first.**

Our tamariki and rangatahi deserve to be loved, nurtured and safe. They should be connected with their whānau, cared for and free to express their authentic selves, no matter where they live. We know we have enough to ensure tamariki are free from poverty and supported through every step of their unique journey. Supporting tamariki means ensuring whānau and communities have everything they need to support their wellbeing.

We have a shared responsibility to make sure tamariki voices are heard, centred and reflected in all decisions that impact them. Tamariki deserve a skilled, well-supported workforce that is trauma informed, culturally responsive and properly trained.

Tamariki Māori are disproportionately impacted by a child protection system that excludes meaningful partnership and underinvests in culturally grounded, whānau-led solutions. A functioning system should centre whakapapa and identity, with whānau and hapū resourced to lead decisions affecting their tamariki.

The Green Party reflects our commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi by addressing the inequities tamariki Māori face in everyday life and in the state care system.

### **Our plan**

1. Legislate so that the child’s voice is central in all decisions that matter to them by using the Child Impact Assessment Tool consistently and fully incorporating the Rights of the Child into legislation.
2. Increase the Best Start payment and extend it to every child under three as a universal child benefit for the early years.
3. Elevate workforce safety by funding training and a workforce development strategy prioritising Māori, Pacific, rainbow, disabled and community provider pathways.
4. Improve access to both diagnosis and support services for children with disabilities or learning support needs.
5. Amend the Oranga Tamariki Act so that it protects tamariki Māori and explicitly embeds whānau participation in decision-making to exercise iwi or hapū authority.

# Climate Action: Resilience and Adaption

### **Keeping Aotearoa safe and prepared**

**The Green Party will prepare all New Zealanders for the impacts of climate change.**

We will ensure that everyone is comprehensively supported through both the transition to a zero emissions economy and increasingly severe weather events like cyclones.

Climate change is one of the biggest challenges of our time. Across Aotearoa, we are already feeling the impacts of more intense and frequent storms, flooding and drought with devastating consequences.

Marae and community groups are often on the frontlines of the emergency and clean-up response, but these groups are not supported by the Government to proactively plan and adapt.

People are worried — about rising insurance prices, and what happens when disaster strikes, particularly those living in increasingly flood and slip exposed areas. They have not received any clarity from the Government about help that might be available down the track when they need it.

Climate change means that some areas are not safe to build in, nor to keep living in, and so retreat is the only safe option in the long term. But again, the Government has failed to help communities facing this uncertain future with any support, plans or guidance.
The Green Party will provide this much-needed clarity.

We will ensure that any National Adaptation Framework is anchored by Te Tiriti o Waitangi. We will support the autonomy and self-determination of hapū, iwi and community organisations to develop and implement their own climate change response plans.

The Green Party will ensure that local government and communities are comprehensively funded to respond to their climate adaptation challenges.

### **Our plan**

1. Ensure climate adaptation planning affirms tino rangatiratanga and upholds the mana motuhake of whānau, hapū and iwi over whenua, wai and taonga by appropriately funding a Māori Climate Resilience Fund.
2. Expand the role of the Natural Hazards Commission to include cover for climate-related weather events and ensure it plays a key role in managing community-led adaptation and retreat.
3. Prioritise long-term, nature-based solutions over short-term engineering solutions, and increase funding for hapū, iwi and community organisations to deliver these.
4. Ensure planning frameworks give effect to the need for climate adaptation in the approach to land and water use, together with supporting ecosystem restoration and conservation.
5. Establish a dedicated fund for central and local government to implement climate adaptation and resilience measures, including funding for partnerships with tangata whenua and community organisations.
6. Scale up support for, and work with, neighbouring countries in the Pacific to adapt to climate change, and advocate for an international agreement on the rights of people displaced by climate change.

# Conservation and Biodiversity

### **Protecting and restoring plants, animals and ecosystems.**

**The Green Party will protect our precious whenua, moana and taonga species from corporate exploitation.**

Aotearoa is home to natural taonga found nowhere else in the world. Our ngahere (forests), awa (rivers) and moana are central to our national identity and way of life.

The Luxon Government has made it easier for corporations to plunder and tear up te taiao (nature), putting private profits ahead of our treasured native wildlife. Meanwhile, many of our native species are on the brink of collapse. Without urgent action, we’re at risk of losing them forever.

The Green Party will work towards protecting 30% of land and oceans because we know the mauri and health of te taiao is foundational to the wellbeing of our people, our climate and our communities. We will achieve this by giving effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi and recognising tangata whenua as the original and ongoing kaitiaki of Aotearoa.

New Zealanders deserve to experience our national parks and hear the calls of our native manu for generations to come. That’s why the Green Party will ensure conservation decisions are made for the public good, not in the interests of private profiteers.

We won’t just restore what’s been lost. We will invest in an Aotearoa where people and nature flourish together.

### **Our plan**

1. Reform conservation and wildlife protection laws to give effect to Te Tiriti, elevate Indigenous-led land stewardship and ensure the conservation management system prioritises halting and reversing nature loss in Aotearoa.
2. Ban new mining on conservation land, including stewardship land.
3. Expand funding for Jobs for Nature – Mahi mō te Taiao to protect our biodiversity and create thousands of regional jobs.
4. Protect all remaining natural wetlands in legislation, including coastal wetlands and estuaries, and implement a plan to restore at least 30% of degraded wetland area, prioritising areas most important for biodiversity recovery and community resilience.
5. Fund Action for Nature, the implementation plan for the biodiversity strategy, and implement national guidance to protect indigenous biodiversity, including the protection of taonga species.
6. Increase overall public conservation funding, including increasing funding and support for the Predator Free 2050 goal.

# Culture and Creativity

### **An Aotearoa that values artists.**

**The Green Party will invest in the arts, creativity and culture that makes Aotearoa vibrant and unique.**

Our art, artists and creatives tell the stories of our communities and help make sense of the world around us.

This government has starved the sector of support. Too many of our creatives are working without the certainty of a stable income, and many lack access to the training and education needed to foster their skills and talents. Steep cuts to Māori arts and broadcasting have left them to scale down or to fend for themselves.

Those governments have seen the arts as a nice-to-have, rather than central to our identity as New Zealanders. They’ve rolled out the red carpet for big overseas studios, sending funds offshore, while local and Indigenous artists are left to struggle.

Arts, culture and creativity are vital for creating vibrant cities and communities. Like other community infrastructure, the arts, culture and creative sectors need proper support.

It is time for artists and creatives to be valued, respected and recognised for their work. The Green Party will fund the arts properly and ensure artists have the long-term sustainability, training and venues that are necessary to build an audience and a meaningful livelihood.

Together, we can support the people behind the books, music, movies, shows and images that tell our stories.

### **Our plan**

1. Require that all publicly funded projects pay at least the living wage to artists, and expand paid artist residencies.
2. Provide stable funding for creative organisations and events such as Te Urungi, including long-term funding for significant creative initiatives such as Te Matatini and Polyfest.
3. Provide sustainable long-term arts funding that is not reliant on gambling revenue, alongside alcohol-free venues for performers.
4. Support and invest in repatriating taonga currently overseas back to iwi, hapū and whānau Māori, as well as keeping taonga in Aotearoa.
5. Establish infrastructure across ministries to strengthen our creative and cultural economy and maximise opportunities for local artists.
6. Increase funding for quality, non-commercial public media that nurtures and promotes our talent and creativity as a nation, including sustainable funding for Radio New Zealand and Whakaata Māori.
7. Increase resourcing for student, community, regional, Māori and Pacific media and radio.

# Democracy

### **Politics for people, not big money.**

**The Green Party will ensure that our democracy represents the people, not wealthy corporate interests.**

Our democracy should work for everyone, not just the wealthy few.

Around the world, democracy is under threat by would-be dictators and corporate power.

Successive governments have meddled with our electoral rules for their own self-interest and failed to curb the influence of big corporate interests in politics.. This government has actively invited those big corporates in to write the rules in their own favour.

The richest few can spend millions trying to influence Ministers, while politicians weaken our donation laws, make it harder to vote and strip thousands of people of their right to vote in breach of their human rights.

The Green Party is committed to a democracy that upholds Te Tiriti o Waitangi and the vision of Matike Mai Aotearoa, creating a decision-making process that reflects genuine partnership.

We can create a more representative democracy by transforming our constitution, expanding voting rights and banning big money from politics.

### **Our plan**

1. Resource a national conversation for constitutional transformation that upholds He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti o Waitangi as our founding constitutional documents, utilising Matike Mai Aotearoa to facilitate community discussions.
2. Uphold the right to vote by extending the voting age to 16, extending the right to vote to all people in custody and restoring enrolment up to election day.
3. Entrench the Māori electoral seats to guarantee Māori representation in Parliament and extend the time in which Māori can switch rolls.
4. Reform electoral funding by limiting donations to registered voters, increasing public financing of campaigns and capping a donor’s donations at a level that does not risk donor influence over policy.
5. Strengthen the rules and transparency over political lobbying, including through a lobbyist register and a code of conduct.

# Digital Technology

### **Technology helping, not harming.**

**The Green Party will hold digital platforms accountable to protect us and our information.**

Digital environments should support our wellbeing, connect our communities, protect our privacy and respect our sovereignty and nature’s limits.

The choices we make on how to deploy and use technology should be under democratic control, not defined for us by overseas corporations who prioritise shareholders over citizens. All of us have been exposed to harmful and toxic content that damages our mental health, weakens trust between people and splinters our shared reality.

Data centres running AI models threaten to suck our energy and clean water sources dry. Intellectual property and Māori culture are exploited and stolen by unaccountable platforms. Companies from social media giants to those storing our health records collect more information about us than required while proving that they can’t be trusted with it.

Many of these platforms have become digital infrastructure necessary to access essential services, yet aren’t adequately regulated nor owned by Aotearoa. Many of us still face barriers to using these platforms at all.

Successive governments have left these platforms alone because they think it’s too hard, or they’ve wasted their time on false solutions.

The Green Party will take a harm-reduction approach to digital technology. We will hold digital platforms accountable to protect us and our information, so all of us can access and enjoy the benefits of digital services without compromising our privacy and our online safety.

### **Our plan**

1. Regulate social media platforms to address harmful content and behaviour by introducing a Digital Duty of Care. This will require algorithmic transparency and accessible and responsive complaints systems, as well as strengthening enforcement with an independent national regulator.
2. Regulate artificial intelligence to ensure its use is safe, transparent and accurate,
   including stronger rules around ‘deepfakes’ and scam material.
3. Crack down on tax avoidance and the offshoring of profits by multinational tech giants such as Meta, Amazon and Microsoft.
4. Adopt and implement the Māori Data Governance Model and Māori AI Governance Framework from Te Kāhui Raraunga across the public sector to protect Māori data sovereignty.
5. Strengthen obligations on data-holders to protect user and biometric data, increase penalties for privacy breaches, and strengthen enforcement powers for the Privacy Commissioner to better protect personal information.
6. Expand media and digital literacy education, and equip New Zealanders to navigate AI-generated media and other emerging digital technologies.
7. Reduce barriers to digital inclusion and ensure all communities have access to the internet, suitable devices and offline alternatives for essential services.

# Disability

### **An accessible Aotearoa for all.**

**The Green Party will build an Aotearoa where disabled people are valued and they and their whānau live with dignity and autonomy.**

An Aotearoa where disabled people and whānau have access to the services they need — like transport and good quality housing — means everyone can thrive in caring communities.

Our current laws, policies and social norms mean disabled people are often denied the same rights as others and are excluded from places and activities non-disabled people take for granted.

These barriers are often worse for tāngata whaikaha Māori and for disabled people from marginalised communities.

The current Government has made it harder for disabled people to access the support they deserve and which enables them to participate equally in life and their communities.

The Green Party is ambitious in its plan to create a more accessible Aotearoa by building on the Enabling Good Lives framework and grounding our approach in Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Our approach will operate on a high-trust model and apply to all disabled people, including those with disabling conditions who do not currently access support.

The Green Party is committed to an Aotearoa where disabled people and whānau thrive in caring communities.

### **Our plan**

1. Introduce a disability rights law based on Te Tiriti with enforceable accessibility standards.
2. Provide easily accessible and timely income support to meet all disability-related living and medical costs, regardless of relationship status and cause of disability.
3. Address homelessness and work towards all disabled people being able to live in safe, accessible, affordable housing in the community of their choice, including by setting robust universal design standards for public and private housing.
4. Make getting around accessible, including by continuing to fund the 75% subsidy for the Total Mobility taxi scheme, making it easier to use and increasing the number of mobility vehicles to meet demand.
5. Draw on the Enabling Good Lives approach to guide how government agencies work with disabled people. Remove barriers to accessing the essentials like health care, transport, inclusive education and disability support for all who need it.
6. Ensure national and local emergency response plans address the needs of disabled people.
7. Uphold legal capacity for everyone, moving from legal capacity assessments to rights-based systems of supported decision-making.

# Drug Law Reform

### **Putting health first to keep people safe.**

**The Green Party will take an evidenced, health-based approach to alcohol and other drugs to reduce harm in our communities.**

Successive governments have tinkered around the edges of our drug laws but largely left them unchanged from the ‘war on drugs’ approach of 50 years ago. Newsflash: they’re losing the war on drugs. This approach has been punitive and has not reduced harm or demand. Instead, it fills our courts and prisons, diverts money away from public health services and leaves frontline services chronically under-resourced. It makes the problem worse.

Drugs exist and people use them. It’s a political decision to either try and reduce the harm that can arise and help make people’s lives safer, or leave people faced with stigma and fear that stops them from reaching out for help.

It’s past time to overhaul our drug laws and replace them with an evidence-based approach that prioritises the health of people. We will increase funding for mental health and addiction services and put a fence up at the top of the cliff, instead of handcuffs at the bottom.

### **Our plan**

1. Repeal and replace the Misuse of Drugs Act with an evidence-based approach that reduces harm, treats drug use as a health issue and provides for regulated access to cannabis for personal use.
2. Ramp up funding of harm reduction and addiction support for people who want to reduce or stop their drug intake, including through kaupapa Māori, rainbow, youth and harm reduction programmes.
3. Work with local government and service providers — focused on safe drug use, addictions and social housing — to support town centres negatively impacted by drug use.
4. Enable a licensing system for psychedelic treatment and recognise taonga status of our native psylocibin (magic mushroom) species.
5. Pass Good Samaritan laws that allow people to call for help without fear of punishment. Legalise and fund other overdose measures including increasing the availability of naloxone and medically supervised consumption spaces to reduce harm and save lives.
6. Fund culturally responsive vaping and smoking cessation services, phase down nicotine availability, and implement stronger regulation and enforcement for nicotine retailers to protect young people and children.
7. Replace the Land Transport (Drug Driving) Amendment Act 2025 with an impairment approach to reduce harm from all causes of driving impairment.
8. Phase out all alcohol advertising and sponsorship, including at sporting and cultural events, and use funding from the alcohol levy to establish a well-resourced national harm-reduction campaign.

# Education

### An Aotearoa where everyone can reach their full potential.

**The Green Party will support an inclusive education system that uplifts everyone.**

Education is a public good and a lifelong right, not a commodity. The Green Party believes education must foster curiosity, creativity and confidence. Education should support every person to discover who they are and how they can contribute to a just, sustainable world.

Education plays a vital role in building social cohesion and democratic life, and should be planned and funded to deliver this. Schools, kura and early learning centres should be places of belonging where diverse cultures, identities and experiences are valued.

Unfortunately, today’s education system treats education as a competitive market and learning as a means to a narrowly defined end. When decisions are driven by standardisation, ranking and market forces, it erodes trust, sidelines creativity and reinforces exclusion.

The Green Party champions an education approach grounded in Te Tiriti o Waitangi and universal human rights, where inclusion is foundational. This system honours tino rangatiratanga, embraces te reo Māori and mātauranga Māori, and ensures Māori voices and communities are central to decision-making. Disabled people, rainbow communities, migrants and refugees, and others facing structural barriers are fully supported to learn, belong and thrive. Educators’ voices and expertise are central to decisions at all levels.

In the well-resourced system we will build, education supports lifelong learning, strengthens wellbeing, and is a force for transformation of individuals, communities and society as a whole.

### **Our plan**

1. Make early childhood education free and provide it as a public good like schooling, removing the market and stopping corporate interests from running for-profit centres.
2. Reset the Government’s rushed and ideological curriculum and assessment reforms, reverting to the original direction of Te Mātaiaho and ensuring qualification reform follows curriculum reform.
3. Expand the criteria for access to learning support. Establish a single agency to coordinate and resource specialist supports for learners with health and disability support needs. Implement all actions in the ‘Framework for Action: A quality education for all’.
4. Expand Ka Ora, Ka Ako as a first step towards providing a warm and nutritious locally made lunch to all schoolchildren.
5. Support rangatiratanga to provide an education system driven by whānau needs, allowing space for whakapapa-based decisions, and working towards a Māori Education Authority governing and funding all Māori medium and Kaupapa Māori education.
6. Support the workforce so all teachers and educators have fair wages and staffing levels that support quality teaching. Co-develop a long-term workforce plan with the sector.

# Energy

### Powering Aotearoa with affordable renewable energy.

**The Green Party will fix our broken power system so that people, not profits, come first.**

Aotearoa can be a nation with energy independence, where everyone has access to affordable, reliable, clean renewable energy. The Green Party will ensure our energy system prioritises public good, so the benefits of our renewable resources stay with people, rather than driving corporate profit.

Our reliance on both fossil fuels and a profit-driven market exposes households to global shocks and rising costs. Instead of fixing these, the current Government has reopened fossil fuel drilling, handed out fossil fuel subsidies and slowed the transition to clean, homegrown energy that we urgently need. Regular people are left paying more for a system that serves corporate interests first.

The Green Party will speed up the electrification of our energy system and fix the rules of the energy market so public wellbeing comes before corporate profits. We will grow renewable generation like wind and solar, support community- and Māori-led energy projects, and improve energy efficiency so homes are warmer and bills are lower. Rural communities and farms can be more resilient, affordable and efficient by shifting to electric powered machines.

By ending our dependence on fossil fuels and putting communities in charge of their energy, we can build a fairer, more resilient future where clean energy is locally controlled and where everyone can afford to warm their homes.

### **Our plan**

1. Put public wellbeing outcomes first in legislation to guarantee the power system works for people, not profits.
2. Establish a renewable energy infrastructure agency to ensure security of supply and lower prices for households, businesses and industry.
3. Increase resilience by enabling greater distributed solar and batteries for households, marae and suitable public buildings, and supporting community-led energy planning.
4. Ban new fossil fuel extraction, end subsidies for fossil fuels and cancel the LNG terminal.
5. Establish a single energy regulator and a Ministry for Energy, focusing on affordable, secure and sustainable energy with equitable access and Te Tiriti-based frameworks that enable Māori and community involvement, ownership and leadership in energy projects.
6. Work with industry to decarbonise and encourage demand response and energy efficiency.

# Environmental Protection

### Protecting and restoring nature.

**The Green Party stands for a healthy environment as the foundation of healthy communities.**

In Aotearoa, our environment is the foundation of our communities and our identity. We all rely on clean rivers for safe drinking water. Our native forests and wetlands help reduce flooding. Healthy soils and abundant oceans provide kai. When our freshwater, native bush and moana thrive, we thrive too.

Luxon’s coalition Government has been the most environmentally damaging in a generation, prioritising private profit at the expense of te taiao (nature).

They have fast-tracked destructive mining projects in wild places and scrapped our Ministry for the Environment. They have changed laws to more easily allow the killing of native wildlife where it stands in the way of development, and allowed rivers, lakes and groundwater to become more polluted. Environmental laws have been gutted, alongside the dismantling of shared decision-making processes that honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

The Green Party will strengthen environmental protections, uphold Te Tiriti and restore te taiao. Protection and restoration of our environment is the foundation of our future.

### **Our plan**

1. Implement strong evidence-based limits for ecosystem health, secure the role of Te Tiriti and affirm the role of tangata whenua as shared decision-makers and kaitiaki in the new resource management system.
2. Repeal the Fast-track Approvals Act and revoke consents for fast-track approvals for new coal, gold and seabed mining projects.
3. Restore a standalone Ministry for the Environment. Increase resources for the Environmental Protection Authority to identify risks to the environment and human health, and for compliance, monitoring and enforcement to ensure polluters are held accountable.
4. Update air quality standards to bring Aotearoa in line with international standards and to protect human health.
5. Work towards eradication of biosecurity incursions, specifically wilding pines, Caulerpa, and yellow-legged hornets.
6. Re-establish resources for the Community Environment Fund to support grassroots environmental education and action.

# Food Fibre and Forestry

### A regenerative approach that puts people and nature first.

**The Green Party will support sustainable farming and forestry that protects our environment, communities and livelihoods.**

We can have a thriving, sustainable food and fibre sector that prioritises mātauranga food production, creates food security, keeps our waterways healthy and provides good jobs for our rural communities.

But for decades, successive governments have encouraged increasingly intensive farming and forestry, prioritising short-term profits over long-term wellbeing. Industrial dairying is our biggest climate polluter and contaminates our drinking water with nitrates. Family-run businesses struggle while large corporate farms profit at the expense of people and planet. Weak rules for forestry have allowed slash to devastate communities when heavy rain hits, damaging homes, infrastructure and waterways. Rural communities are left to clean up the mess.

Solutions exist. The Green Party has campaigned for decades to feed our communities, while reducing the negative impacts of agriculture on nature and the climate. We championed a new regulatory approach to help the organic sector grow.

It’s time to support Aotearoa to shift to regenerative farming and forestry. The Green Party will help farmers phase down intensive practices and ensure the forestry sector can provide good jobs, while also protecting communities and waterways.

### **Our plan**

1. Increase support for farmers to transition to more sustainable forms of agricultural production through finance mechanisms such as low-interest loans and grants.
2. Back Aotearoa-grown natural fibres, including wool, by using them in the construction and refurbishment of schools and public buildings, and establishing a contestable fund for sustainable fibre manufacturing and innovation.
3. Ban palm kernel expeller and ensure all supplementary feed is sustainably sourced and does not strain the carrying capacity of the local environment.
4. Prevent land from being used beyond its capacities by implementing strong controls on clear-fell of plantation forestry, working to transition extremely erosion-prone land to indigenous forestry and establishing a National Soil Strategy that sets direction on soil use, policies and research.
5. Support the local wood processing sector to manufacture higher-value timber products from plantation forestry, such as cross-laminated timber for construction and turning slash into solid biofuels, retaining regional employment and development.
6. Work with Māori-led forestry organisations to support investment in forestry and restoration of forests on whenua Māori and recognise tangata whenua customary use rights in indigenous forestry according to their tīkanga.
7. Establish a biodiversity credits scheme that supports landowners to undertake restoration and protection of land as a voluntary revenue alternative to the Emissions Trading Scheme. As part of this, prioritise marginal whenua Māori where agreed by landowners.

# Freshwater

### Healthy water for drinking, swimming and gathering kai.

**The Green Party will put the health of freshwater and communities first.**

Our rivers and lakes should be clean and teeming with life. Everyone should be able to turn on their tap knowing their water is safe to drink, swim in their local awa (river) without getting sick and fish or gather kai from waterways. Clean, healthy freshwater is the foundation of the health of our people and our environment.

Aotearoa has lost most of its wetlands, and many of our lakes and rivers are in extremely poor health. Luxon’s coalition Government has accelerated this decline by scrapping many protections for freshwater, stopping council plans to restore waterways and weakening standards for wastewater discharges. Meanwhile, many communities can’t drink what comes out of their tap, face regular boil water notices or can’t swim in their local awa.

These have been deliberate choices to prioritise a wealthy few over the wellbeing of everyone. While polluters profit, communities pay the price through unsafe drinking water, polluted swimming holes and native fish like whitebait and tuna (eels) are threatened with extinction.

The Green Party will reverse the decline in the health of our freshwater with strong controls on pollution, support for more sustainable farming, and action to restore wetlands, lakes, and rivers. We will ensure everyone has access to safe drinking water.

### **Our plan**

1. Implement strong, evidence-based national bottom lines for freshwater for both human health and ecosystem health to address pollution including lowering the nitrate limit for drinking water.
2. Reinstate Te Mana o Te Wai to prioritise the health of freshwater in decision-making and regulation and to give effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
3. End all subsidies and public funding for big new irrigation and dam projects and review resource consents where water levels have dropped too far to support a healthy river.
4. Strengthen environmental performance rules for wastewater discharges to ensure lakes, rivers, beaches and coastal areas remain swimmable.
5. Ensure the drinking water regulator is funded and given the mandate for robust and transparent monitoring, reporting and enforcement in the protection of drinking water sources.
6. Support greater resilience from floods by increasing funding for adaptation and allowing for a ‘room for rivers’ approach and using natural systems like wetlands to protect communities.
7. Phase out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser and take action to reduce stocking rates on a catchment basis to improve the health of rivers and drinking water and reduce climate pollution.

# Gender Equity

### For a more equal Aotearoa.

**The Green Party will take action to advance gender equality and ensure women and gender minorities are respected and treated fairly.**

Aotearoa has made decent progress to make this reality come to fruition, but we have a way to go before women and gender minorities can be truly equal in this country. Life is unfair and unsafe for too many – single mothers are vulnerable to hardship and homelessness, gender-based violence is increasing, and women continue to get paid less than men for equal work.

Changes the coalition Government have made have worsened the position of many women and gender minorities. The Government’s changes to pay equity shifted the goal posts and balanced their budget on the backs of our lowest paid working women. Wāhine Māori are overrepresented in the justice system for crimes of poverty, worsened by the coalition Government’s policies. Gender minorities have been attacked and used as a political distraction by Government parties.

The Green Party are proud of our legacy championing solutions to the inequities women and gender minorities face. In Government we championed the first-ever plan to eliminate family violence and sexual violence, Te Aorerekura. We worked with the former Government on pay equity legislation, getting ACC to cover birth injuries, and extending parental leave.

But there is more to do. We will undo the Government’s changes to pay equity to ensure working women are paid fairly. We will work with wāhine Māori to address disparities and injustices in health, justice, work and pay, learning from the ongoing Mana Wāhine Waitangi Tribunal inquiry. We will fund treatment and diagnosis of pelvic pain including endometriosis and properly resource front-line organisations to end family and sexual violence in Aotearoa.

Ensuring women and gender minorities are safe, respected and valued in Aotearoa benefits all of us. The time to act is now.

### **Our plan**

1. Close the gender and ethnic pay gaps by undoing the Government’s changes to the pay equity regime and resuming claims, pay transparency measures, and comprehensive pay gap reporting.
2. Increase the Best Start payment and extend it to every child under three as a universal child benefit for the early years.
3. Fund one-stop-shops that provides pā harakeke wrap-around services for whānau throughout hapūtanga, after birth, first stages of life, and navigating parenthood.
4. Work towards diagnosing and treating endometriosis faster, including by developing formal clinical guidelines for diagnosing and treating endometriosis and other pelvic pain, and by funding specialised clinics across Aotearoa.
5. Resource kaupapa Māori solutions and community-led solutions to family and sexual violence, that have have been developed by disproportionately impacted groups, including women, Pasifika, rainbow, and disabled communities.
6. Amend the Crimes Act to criminalise coercive control, amend the definition of consent, and preclude a defence of reluctant consent to affirm that consent must be free and voluntary, and can be withdrawn at any time while ensuring these changes cause no further harm.
7. Increase paid parental leave to 15 months for the primary caregiver, with additional ring-fenced leave for partners, while also increasing payments.

# Global Affairs and Trade

### A safer, greener, fairer future for people and planet.

**The Green Party will ensure that Aotearoa always stands up for what’s right on the world stage.**

Aotearoa can be a global voice for peace, freedom, democracy, justice, global solidarity and collective action on climate change.

Unfortunately, every corner of our planet is threatened by war, the climate crisis and the rise of authoritarian regimes.

Aotearoa was once an independent voice against nuclear weapons and American militarism. But the Luxon Government has instead turned a blind eye to atrocities and authoritarians and has deepened our military integration with the United States.

Aotearoa must challenge the imperialist ambitions of aspiring powers that plunge the lives of ordinary people into chaos and hardship — not join them.

The Green Party will take an independent and principled approach to foreign affairs and trade that sees Aotearoa leading the world on climate action, nature protection and Indigenous and human rights.

We will work with our Pacific neighbours to create a safer, greener, more just world. Together, we must uphold the international rules of law and our collective obligations for each other and the planet.

The Green Party will always work to support communities facing conflict, human rights abuses, the destruction of nature and the worsening impacts of climate change.

### **Our plan**

1. Restore an independent foreign policy that stands against human rights abuses wherever they occur and upholds peace and justice.
2. Focus defence policy on climate change responses, humanitarian responses and environmental monitoring.
3. Decouple military and security frameworks from the United States, including declining to participate in AUKUS and withdrawing from Five Eyes.
4. Support Pacific sovereignty and independence and oppose the militarisation of the Pacific.
5. Recognise Palestine as a state and sanction Israel.
6. Stand with decolonisation and democracy movements globally, especially those of Indigenous peoples in our Asia–Pacific region.
7. Implement the Trade For All agenda, including democratic scrutiny of trade agreements, and enforceable recognition of our Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations, workers’ rights, human rights and climate commitments.
8. Urgently progress climate change initiatives through international institutions, which include reducing patent protections on green technologies and negotiating an international approach to climate border adjustments.
