# Health

### Accessible care to support everyone’s good health.

**The Green Party will ensure our health care system is equitable, accessible and properly supported.**

Aotearoa has enough to ensure that everyone, everywhere can access timely health care from a supported workforce.

But for years successive governments have underinvested in health services, leading to lengthy wait times and unsafe conditions for the health workers who look after us. Hospitals are understaffed, and GP clinics — important for helping people stay well, not just get better — are so stretched they are closing their doors to new enrolments.

The current Government has reversed decades of progress to provide equitable health care for Māori. Māori are forced into a health system that underserves them and is misaligned with their hauora aspirations.

Private provider costs are locking whānau out of primary health care. This causes health issues to unnecessarily escalate because they are not detected early. Hauora Māori and social service providers are underfunded and restricted by overly prescriptive contracts.

Good health allows all of us to live enjoyable, meaningful lives. The Green Party will expand access to essential primary and dental care. We will work with and fund kaupapa Māori approaches to end health inequities.

Our plans for children, housing, incomes, energy and transport will all support people to keep well by ensuring everyone can access safe, warm homes, nutritious kai and a transport system that encourages active ways of getting around.

It’s time to put a fence at the top of the cliff and support people so they don’t have to rely on ambulances at the bottom.

### **Our plan**

1. Ensure public health care services are accessible for all with a focus on prevention and early screening, diagnosis and treatment for non-communicable diseases, such as kidney disease, cancers, diabetes and cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.
2. Fund mobile health care and mental health care clinics, diagnostics services and dental vans to ensure rural communities are able to access health services regularly, including during and after civil emergencies.
3. Work towards a publicly delivered, fully free provision of dental and primary care services, including by-Māori for-Māori community clinics.
4. Fund one-stop-shops that provides pā harakeke wrap-around services for whānau throughout hapūtanga, after birth, first stages of life, and navigating parenthood.
5. Stop overly prescriptive Hauora service contracts and commit to working with Iwi Māori Partnership Boards and Hauora Māori to simplify and improve funding arrangements for providers of health services for whānau, hapū iwi and hapori.
6. Increase sustained funding for Pharmac so that it can invest in new medicines and health care devices to enhance treatment outcomes and quality of life.
7. Expand the Minor Health Conditions Service to help pharmacies treat common health issues and update the Integrated community pharmacy services agreement to encourage pharmacists to give appropriate medical advice by compensating them fairly.
8. Ensure all health care workers have fair wages, fund pay parity for primary care nurses and hauora providers, and set safe staffing levels to support worker wellbeing and quality of care for patients.
9. Work towards diagnosing and treating endometriosis faster, including by developing formal clinical guidelines for diagnosing and treating endometriosis and other pelvic pain, and by funding specialised clinics across Aotearoa.
10. Increase funding for data and digital infrastructure and capability in the health sector, and regulate and hold private providers of infrastructure to high standards of privacy.

# Housing

### Safe, warm, affordable homes for everyone.

**The Green Party is the only party with a credible plan to ensure everyone can afford a warm and safe place to call home.**

We all need somewhere to call home — a place to rest, to share with our loved ones, to make a life or to watch our kids grow up.

A warm, safe home is a basic right. But successive governments have allowed housing to become a get-rich scheme for a lucky few, and a source of misery and expense for hundreds of thousands of others.

Far too many families are forced to pay through the roof to rent homes that make us sick, and a generation has been locked out of ever owning their own home. This didn’t happen by accident.

It is the consequence of decisions made by successive governments to privilege the wealthy few at our expense.

The Green Party will fix renting to make healthy homes affordable for all of us, and put the interests of people before those of property speculators and investment landlords. We will build thousands more warm, sustainable and affordable homes in the places people want to live.

### **Our plan**

1. Build tens of thousands of new public homes, significantly increase accessible public housing stock and fund more papakāinga to be built on whenua Māori.
2. Make rents more affordable by limiting annual rent increases to no more than 2%, and link rents in a new tenancy to what the previous tenants paid.
3. Strengthen the Healthy Homes Standards and enforce them with an independently certified Rental Warrant of Fitness.
4. Expand immediate wraparound support such as housing first, transitional and supported housing services, and guarantee same-day accommodation placement for people experiencing homelessness.
5. Require councils to collaborate with communities, including mana whenua, to provide sustainable, walkable, mixed-use urban areas and enable enough new affordable homes within existing urban areas to meet the needs of the next generation.
6. Reverse generous tax benefits for landlords and property speculators that encourage housing to be treated as an investment, rather than a basic right.

# Immigration and Community Safety

### Welcoming, safe and fair pathways to make Aotearoa home.

**The Green Party will make sure that everyone who comes to Aotearoa is treated with respect and dignity.**

Migrant workers are not disposable, and deserve a fair go to settle in Aotearoa. If any one of us feared for our life or our family or strived for a better life, we’d hope that we’d be supported to take that big step.

But because of the rules put in place by successive governments, too many migrants and refugees are exploited, denied basic rights and unfairly targeted by immigration compliance officers.

Meanwhile, multimillionaire investors are exempt from many of the same immigration requirements that stop ordinary workers from putting roots down in their community.

The current coalition Government wants you to turn against your migrant neighbour, instead of the billionaires wrecking the planet.

The Green Party will create fair and achievable pathways to residency for all people coming here to work, ensure nobody is unfairly separated from their families or their communities, and scrap the rules that fuel exploitation and abuse.

The Green Party will ensure that asylum seekers arriving in Aotearoa after escaping war or persecution are treated with dignity, and supported to rebuild their lives as part of our communities.

### **Our plan**

1. Create residence pathways for migrants who have settled long-term, including for people living in Aotearoa whose visas have expired.
2. Abolish the Acceptable Standards of Health requirements, so that migrants and refugees are not discriminated against based on their health conditions or disabilities.
3. Allow migrant work visa holders to switch employers and remove the 12-month stand-down period that requires workers to leave Aotearoa between visas.
4. Unite families by clearing the backlog for refugee family reunification, expanding work rights for partners, restoring birthright citizenship and removing income barriers to sponsoring a parent visa.
5. Implement Māori aspirations for an immigration system based on Te Tiriti, including devolving resources and decision-making to hapū and iwi to strengthen traditional whanaungatanga connections. Provide Te Tiriti education to new migrants and refugees.
6. Progressively increase the refugee quota to 5,000 by 2029, increase funding for refugee resettlement programmes and create a humanitarian visa for family of New Zealanders in conflict zones.
7. Resource Immigration New Zealand to clear tier 1 and tier 2 family reunification categories and process asylum claims quickly, and stop the unjust detention and electronic monitoring of asylum seekers.

# Income

### Liveable incomes made possible through a fair tax system.

**The Green Party will guarantee a decent income for all and pay for it with a fair tax system.**

No matter what we do or where we live, everyone should have enough to put food on the table, a safe place to call home and the ability to live a good life.

There is enough for everyone to be well, but right now, thousands of children are going to bed hungry. Families are struggling to pay the rent or mortgage and keep their homes warm. Students are forced to skip meals to make ends meet. The cost of living is only getting tougher under this Government.

The resources we need to lift every family out of poverty are already there. But the Luxon Government has prioritised tax cuts for wealthy landlords and their rich corporate mates instead. This is a political choice.

The Green Party will transform our social welfare systems and create tens of thousands of jobs, so families are looked after at every stage of life.

The Green Party will guarantee a liveable income for everyone. Whether you’re in work, unemployed, disabled, sick, a caregiver or a student, we will ensure you can pay the bills and live a decent life. We can pay for it by making big corporations and the wealthy few pay their fair share in tax.

### **Our plan**

1. Reform the Social Security Act to uphold the dignity of those who need support and ensure everyone has a secure income and a decent standard of living. Implement a high-trust operating model at Work and Income.
2. Increase benefits to liveable rates, individualise benefit entitlements and abolish benefit sanctions.
3. Extend ACC to cover income support and treatment for injuries, disability and illnesses regardless of origin.
4. Strengthen Working for Families by boosting the rate, reducing abatements and extending tax credits to families who are out of work.
5. Make income tax settings fair and progressive, by introducing a tax-free threshold, reducing tax rates for low- and middle-income earners, and increasing the top rate of income tax.
6. Introduce a super-rich tax of 2.5% on net wealth over $10 million so that multimillionaires pay their fair share.
7. Overhaul recoverable assistance so that grants are available for urgent needs instead of loans. Work towards writing off existing debt to MSD and ban attachment orders against beneficiaries.

# Justice and Community Safety

### Keeping communities safe through prevention and rehabilitation.

**The Green Party will make our communities safer by addressing the drivers of crime.**

Our approach is to prevent harm happening in the first place. We will reform the justice system to make it fair, just and equitable.

The current Government’s approach of packing prisons, restricting what judges can decide and neglecting much-needed rehabilitation only causes more harm and hardship.

Our communities are safer when everyone, especially young people, have access to the basics: food, health care, inclusive education, adequate incomes and a safe home environment.

The Green Party will keep our communities safe by prioritising rehabilitation, strengthening true accountability and tackling bias and discrimination in the justice system. Our policies to provide mental health and addiction services, safe and warm housing, and adequate incomes for all will help to address the root causes of crime.

Each person deserves to live free from violence, harm and discrimination. People should not be punished for being poor. We need a justice system that supports this basic premise.

### **Our plan**

1. Resource evidence-based rehabilitation for anyone convicted of an offence, and ensure tikanga-based and restorative justice solutions (such as Te Pae Oranga) are available to anyone who wishes to access these.
2. Expand Te Ao Mārama to all courts in Aotearoa, and ensure specialist youth courts including the Rangatahi and Pasifika Courts, Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Court, and New Beginnings Court are available to all who wish to access them.
3. End military-style academies, raise the age of criminal responsibility and ban the detention of young people in the company of adults in all circumstances.
4. Require body cameras for frontline police, strengthen powers for the Independent Police Conduct Authority, deliver de-escalation and trauma training for police, and increase resourcing for Māori Wardens and Pacific Wardens.
5. Improve community reintegration support for people leaving the criminal justice system, including housing, and increase the Steps to Freedom Grant to cover at least 30 years of inflation.
6. Extend legal aid and duty lawyers, better resource community law centres and make applications for protection and parenting orders free.
7. Enable judicial discretion in sentencing, including by abolishing mandatory minimum sentences, life sentences, preventive detention, limits on sentence discounts, three strikes and limits on when home detention can be imposed instead of imprisonment.
8. Implement the recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Terrorist Attack on Christchurch Mosques on 15 March 2019. Extend hate speech laws to cover religion, gender, disability and rainbow communities. Continue to oppose possession of military-style semi-automatic firearms.
9. Implement all recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, in consultation with people with lived experience.

# Local Government

### Empowering local democracy.

**The Green Party will back local government to deliver community wellbeing.**

Local government plays a vital role in shaping everyday life. When local democracy is strong, communities are stronger too.

Unfortunately, local government is under strain. Councils face growing financial pressure. Democratic engagement is declining and tino rangatiratanga is often sidelined in community decision-making.

At the same time, councils are the frontline of many challenges we face, from climate change to a lack of affordable homes. They are being loaded with new responsibilities — like emergency management — without the proper funding or support to do the job.

This has left councils forced to increase rates and charges to cover basic costs, when communities are already struggling with the high cost of living.

The Green Party will strengthen local democracy and rebuild trust in local decision-making through fairer elections, stronger participation and more community-led processes. We will provide fair and sustainable funding tools, and ensure community wellbeing is at the heart of what local government delivers.

We will work with local government — not against it — and treat councils with the respect they deserve as the democratic voice of their communities. By backing local democracy, we can ensure decisions are made by communities, not for them.

### **Our plan**

1. Strengthen local electoral democracy by transferring administration of local government elections to the Electoral Commission, enabling 16-year-olds to vote and requiring the use of a single transferable voting system.
2. Reinforce councils’ responsibility to give effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi by making the role of local government as a Te Tiriti partner explicit, and reinstate their ability to keep Māori wards for their districts.
3. Reject the proposed rates cap and enable a range of new funding and financing tools, such as a bed levy, congestion charging and GST from rates and growth.
4. Ensure that the ‘four wellbeings’ (social, economic, environmental and cultural) are core to the purpose of local government and empower councils by devolving further responsibilities from central government, with appropriate resourcing.
5. Enable greater use of community-based decision-making processes — such as citizens’ assemblies — including greater community input in the process for local government reorganisation.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-maori-centr.title: Māori Centred
documents/web-manifesto-2026-maori-centr.text:
# Māori Centred

### By Māori, for Māori.

**The Green Party will support Māori to make decisions about the destiny of their own whānau, hapū and iwi.**

Tangata whenua lived undisturbed for centuries as hapū, creating tikanga unique to the whenua and focusing on the health and sustainability of their whakapapa. When tangata whenua thrive, so does everyone who lives in Aotearoa. Supporting ongoing kaupapa Māori approaches for Māori to fulfil their aspirations was affirmed and guaranteed by Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

When Te Tiriti was signed, it was assured that the relationship between tangata whenua and the Crown would mean no change in the way Māori choose to live their lives. However, successive governments continue to implement harmful actions which have eroded Māori social structures, contributed to the loss of traditional knowledge and created intergenerational inequities across many key metrics.

The current Government’s legislative assaults have targeted tangata whenua from all sides. They have consistently ignored independent experts, the Waitangi Tribunal and their own advisors, who have warned that their actions will only deepen existing inequities and contribute to further racial divides.

It is time to remove the burden from Māori to keep reminding the Crown of their promises. The Crown must take accountability for their ongoing injustices against Te Tiriti and for using te iwi Māori as a political football.

The Green Party supports tangata whenua-led processes, actions and decision-making by devolving power and investing resources in all matters that affect Māori. We know that Te Tiriti and democracy are not contradictory, but complementary.

Returning whenua to its kaitiaki, and facilitating ‘by Māori, for Māori’ solutions to target inequities are ways we can uphold Te Tiriti while honouring the democracy that Aotearoa should be founded on.

### **Our plan**

1. Devolve power and redistribute resources back to tangata whenua in recognition that Māori are the decision-makers and facilitators of the destiny of their own whānau, hapū and iwi.
2. Invest in outcomes that minimise the disparities and inequities tangata whenua face across the majority of social and economic outcomes.
3. Resource marae through a Marae Resilience Fund for Māori to lead initiatives for their people, wāhi tapu (sacred sites) and whenua in accordance with their own tikanga. Create ongoing funding for provisions for civil emergencies in recognition of being consistent community lifelines.
4. End perpetual leases on whenua Māori and amend the Public Works Act to prevent the acquisition of Māori freehold land, Māori customary land and lands within a reasonable proximity to marae, urupā and wāhi tapu.
5. Expand the learning, speaking and promotion of te reo Māori in both formal and informal settings to encourage the widespread use of the language across the nation.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-mental-heal.title: Mental Health
documents/web-manifesto-2026-mental-heal.text:
# Mental Health

### A safe, supportive and accessible care system.

**The Green Party will work to address the drivers of poor mental health, and ensure everyone can get safe, culturally relevant care when they need it.**

Aotearoa should be a place where anyone in distress can access support, no matter where they are.

But right now, demand is skyrocketing, services are fragmented and workforce shortages are leading to long wait times and staff burnout. Prioritising private care in the mental health sector has led to increased costs and wait times too.

Our high rates of social inequality, child poverty, family violence, homelessness and climate anxiety are driving mental distress in our communities, particularly for young people.

It doesn’t have to be this way. We have the tools to support liveable incomes, provide trauma support and end homelessness in this country to promote better mental health. We know what we need to do to face the existential threat of climate change head-on.

The Green Party will expand free services so cost is never a barrier. We will provide more funding to kaupapa Māori and Māori centred youth services so care is culturally relevant to our communities.

The mental health workforce will receive more support, staffing and funding to reduce burnout. This will allow harmful practices like seclusion to be phased out, to ensure acute mental health care is rehabilitative, not harmful.

### **Our plan**

1. Expand free mental health services to all communities so everyone can access support when they need it. This includes expanding youth services like Piki, Mana Ake and Youth One Stop Shops throughout Aotearoa, Asian Family Services and dedicated support for postnatal mental health.
2. Implement the recommendations of the Every Life Matters – He Tapu te Oranga o ia Tangata Suicide Prevention Strategy, together with further actions identified as part of the kaupapa Māori response to suicide prevention with particular focus on people under 24.
3. Implement community care models and ensure mental health facilities are resourced adequately to enable phasing out the use of seclusion (solitary confinement) entirely, and increase the availability of early intervention to reduce the use of compulsory care.
4. Fund kaupapa Māori mental health and addiction programmes and ensure rangatahi Māori voice is represented in policy.
5. Link primary health and secondary mental health services with clear referral pathways in every health region and focus on areas which have disproportionate need.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-.title: Oceans and Fisheries
documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-.text:
# Oceans and Fisheries

### Abundant oceans teeming with kaimoana.

**The Green Party will restore the mauri (life force) of our moana through bold marine protection initiatives.**

The vast moana surrounding Aotearoa is a taonga. New Zealanders deserve to have healthy and thriving oceans, with abundant marine life that provides sustainable kaimoana.

Right now, our oceans are under severe stress. Overfishing, destructive bottom trawling, plastic pollution and climate change have driven marine ecosystems towards collapse. Iconic species like tipa (scallops) and koura (crayfish) are now functionally extinct in some places. Across the country, whole communities can’t access local kaimoana because decades of overfishing has plundered stocks for profit.

The current Government has relentlessly prioritised short-term commercial profits over long-term ocean health. They have cut industry levies, allowed fishing in high-protection areas, delayed bans on bottom trawling and proposed drastic changes that would reverse our fisheries regulations.

The Green Party will always put the health of our oceans above corporate interests. We will place Te Tiriti o Waitangi at the centre of our approach to restoring the abundance of our moana. We will work towards every New Zealander enjoying the right to gather kaimoana and experiencing abundant marine life for generations to come.

### **Our plan**

1. Protect at least 30% of New Zealand’s ocean territory by 2030 through reforming marine protected areas legislation to ensure it is fit for purpose and enables both tikanga-led tools consistent with Te Tiriti, and approaches to improve ocean health outcomes.
2. Phase out damaging fishing methods, starting by banning bottom trawling on seamounts, and banning set netting and dredging.
3. Ban seabed mining in the coastal marine area and the exclusive economic zone and maintain pressure for a moratorium on seabed mining in international waters.
4. Embed kaitiakitanga Māori in marine policy and operational management. Resource iwi and hapū to lead oceans protection and implement mātauranga- and tikanga-based projects for ocean conservation.
5. Reduce fisheries bycatch of protected species by ensuring cameras are rolled out on the entire fishing fleet and by setting fisheries-related mortality limits.
6. Ratify the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction and support marine protection proposals in the high seas, Southern Ocean and throughout the Pacific.
7. Review the Quota Management System and move towards an ecosystem-based fisheries management model, in line with the Māori fisheries settlements.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-overseas-ne.title: Overseas New Zealanders
documents/web-manifesto-2026-overseas-ne.text:
# Overseas New Zealanders

### Cultivating Kiwi connections around the world.

**The Green Party will ensure all New Zealanders living overseas can feel connected to home.**

More and more New Zealanders are leaving for overseas, particularly as a result of the current Government’s choices.

The Luxon Government has forgotten that they are supposed to represent the 15% of New Zealanders who live overseas too. While the cost of living has hit hard around the world, they decided to increase interest rates on student loans for New Zealanders overseas, making it harder for them to come home.

The Green Party understands that Aotearoa is about all its people, wherever in the world they are. We will ensure everyone living overseas is meaningfully connected to home, and can continue to have a say in our democracy. We will support tangata whenua to ensure they can always return to their turangawaewae, no matter where they were born.

Wherever we are in the world, Aotearoa is a special place that we should all feel connected to. It’s time we took a compassionate approach to all our whānau living overseas.

### **Our plan**

1. Enable a tikanga-based pathway for people who whakapapa Māori to establish Aotearoa citizenship, regardless of country of residence or birth.
2. Reduce and re-balance student loan repayments and interest rates for overseas student loan borrowers, extend the repayment holiday for overseas borrowers, and abolish border arrests for student loan repayment violations.
3. Extend the time that overseas New Zealanders can spend outside Aotearoa without losing voting eligibility.
4. Restore the 10-year period for time spent in Aotearoa New Zealand to be eligible for superannuation.
5. Pursue reciprocal health care, welfare support and visa waiver arrangements with other countries, and widen existing agreements to include temporary visitors.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-pacific-peo.title: Pacific Peoples
documents/web-manifesto-2026-pacific-peo.text:
# Pacific Peoples

### Deepening connections and uplifting communities.

**The Green Party will strengthen the relationship between Aotearoa and the Pacific through partnership grounded in respect, reciprocity and shared prosperity.**

Aotearoa stands as a Pacific nation, grounded in deep and enduring whakapapa connections with Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa.

Pacific Peoples are central to our shared future. Their innovation, leadership and cultural intelligence will help shape a sustainable, inclusive and thriving Aotearoa.

Pacific Peoples are one of our most youthful and fastest-growing communities, yet systemic barriers mean too many face challenges in employment, housing, education and health. Current visa rules make it hard for Pacific people to visit their family here in Aotearoa. Too many Pacific workers are denied the dignity, protections and fair conditions they deserve.

Persistent inequities and underinvestment threaten to hold back prosperity and undermine our relationship with the wider Pacific. The current Government has cut climate aid funding and slashed targeted funding for Pacific initiatives.

This term the Green Party helped restore citizenship for thousands of Samoans by passing the Citizenship (Western Samoa Restoration) Amendment Act, securing a historic win for Pacific justice. But there is still much more work to do.

It’s time for Aotearoa to show our Pacific identity with meaningful action that uplifts Pacific leadership, strengthens communities and deepens our relationships across Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa.

### **Our plan**

1. Extend visa-free travel to Aotearoa for visitors from the Pacific Islands.
2. Restore and increase the international climate aid funding Aotearoa contributes. Affirm and support calls by Pacific Island nations for stronger climate action in international negotiations.
3. Resource tangata moana leadership on climate action within Aotearoa.
4. Replace the Recognised Seasonal Employer Scheme with an alternative that gives Pacific workers access to fair wages, housing and essential services, and provides for open work rights and residency pathways rather than being tied to a single employer.
5. Support the independence of West Papua and French-occupied Polynesia. Call for an Indigenous-led human rights investigation and a visit from the Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
6. Support Pacific Island states with their marine protection initiatives, including by increasing funding support for the South Pacific Regional Environment Programme and supporting marine protected areas in the Pacific Ocean under the High Seas Treaty.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-public-serv.title: Public Services
documents/web-manifesto-2026-public-serv.text:
# Public Services

### Strong essential services accessible to everyone.

**The Green Party will make sure that public services support the public good.**

Investing in public services means investing in all of us. Public services are the way we make sure every person, whānau and community can live with dignity, security and real opportunity — not just those who can afford to pay.

For too long, underinvestment and privatisation have left essential systems stretched, fragmented and harder to access. Public services should be treated as investments in our shared future, not costs to cut. The Green Party will ensure that health care, education, housing, infrastructure and support for families are recognised as public goods that are planned and funded to meet people’s needs, not shaped around private profit.

Aotearoa has enough to properly invest in the services and infrastructure everyone relies on and to ensure these services stay in public hands. Strong public services also require a strong, capable and independent public sector with a commitment to uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Aotearoa can have an economy that works for all of us, where collective resources are used to improve quality of life, care for te taiao and give every community what it needs to thrive.

### **Our plan**

1. Uphold Te Tiriti throughout the work of the public service, and fund Māori organisations, iwi, hapū and marae to run community and environmental initiatives that meet the needs and aspirations unique to their rohe (region).
2. Fund public services adequately to ensure that they are able to work in service of the public good, and that public services (and state-owned enterprises) remain in public hands.
3. Reform the public finance system to ensure that the fiscal management approach supports New Zealand’s long-term resilience, the productive capacity of our economy, and an ensures the health and well-being of everyone.
4. Affirm the importance of advocacy and monitoring done by independent commissions with expertise in an area, starting with restoring the monitoring role of the Children’s Commissioner alongside its advocacy function.
5. Introduce standardised career progression, pay, community secondment opportunities and training across the public sector to improve staff retention and skills development, and ensure equal pay for equivalent roles.
6. Provide secure, flexible and full funding arrangements for the community sector, recognising the value of the work, and ensuring independence within a supportive legislative framework.
7. Improve training in Te Tiriti and te reo Māori for all public servants, resulting in consistency across all agencies.
8. Ensure that the public service is a leader in disability-responsive employment, including by providing resources and training to meet access needs and counter ableism.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-rainbow-com.title: Rainbow Communities
documents/web-manifesto-2026-rainbow-com.text:
# Rainbow Communities

### Rainbow communities thriving with freedom, equality and respect.

**The Green Party will nurture an Aotearoa where everyone belongs and enjoys a safe, healthy and happy life.**

All New Zealanders deserve to live with dignity, safety and the freedom to be themselves in a community where they belong. For takatāpui, rainbow, MVPFAFF+ and Pacific LGBTQI+, trans, non-binary and intersex people, this means more than symbolic support.

It means celebrating the joy of rainbow communities as well as addressing the inequities many experience. It means our public services must care for, include and uphold the mana of rainbow people. The deeply connected relationships between rainbow identities, whakapapa and whānau must also be acknowledged and allowed to thrive.

Barriers that stop people participating fully in their communities must be removed. Some Rainbow communities — including takatāpui, MVPFAFF+ and Pacific LGBTQI+ communities, disabled rainbow people, migrants, refugees, young people and intersex people — face overlapping and compounding barriers to a healthy life that must be recognised and addressed.

The Green Party believes that rainbow health care should be shaped by compassion, evidence and aroha — not fear or political division.

Decisions that affect communities should be made with them, not imposed on them. The Green Party will put people at the heart of political decision-making, ensuring those most impacted by policy are heard.

### **Our plan**

1. Work with the different rainbow communities to develop appropriate health care services and strategies built cultural values and holistic models of care and wellbeing.
2. Increase resourcing for rainbow organisations, including dedicated support for Māori and Pasifika-led organisations, to support the development and delivery of services that reflect the diverse needs, values, and strengths of rainbow communities.
3. Resource clear pathways for timely, free, non-discriminatory access to all forms of gender-affirming health care based on informed consent and self-determination, including reversal of the ban on puberty blockers.
4. Promote the human rights of takatāpui, intersex and rainbow people, amending the Human Rights Act to clarify that all forms of sexual orientation, gender identity and variations in sex characteristics, are prohibited grounds of discrimination, and implement the Law Commission’s Ia Tangata report recommendations.
5. Prohibit all non-consensual and medically unnecessary surgeries or medical interventions on intersex people.
6. Reform laws and policies so rainbow asylum seekers, refugees and migrants can access legal gender recognition, partnership recognition, family reunification, and resettlement support.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-seniors.md.title: Seniors
documents/web-manifesto-2026-seniors.md.text:
# Seniors

### Happy, healthy and supported.

**The Green Party will uphold the mana of seniors by prioritising the support that enables equitable and fulfilling lives.**

Seniors have cared for us and served their communities. Many continue to do so during retirement.

Every senior should be valued, connected and able to live with dignity. However, the Luxon Government has sidelined the needs of seniors, meaning many find themselves without the care and support they need. Some have no one to turn to.

Guided by manaakitanga, whanaungatanga, and led by Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we envision communities where seniors are recognised and celebrated as leaders and knowledge holders, actively shaping whānau, hapū and iwi life. Homes are warm, accessible and designed for connection across generations, while community spaces and marae-based centres foster belonging, learning and support.

We believe those who work in aged care must be respected and rewarded, with secure conditions that enable them to provide high-quality, compassionate support. Care systems should be equitable, culturally grounded, and responsive, ensuring Māori, Pacific Peoples and diverse communities can access services that reflect their values and tikanga.

The Green Party commits to a long-term, non-partisan vision where seniors thrive with dignity and autonomy in vibrant intergenerational communities, ensuring that ageing is a positive process.

### **Our plan**

1. Launch a dedicated long-term strategy for the needs of an ageing population which encompasses the holistic wellbeing of kaumātua, elder abuse prevention, ensuring income is equitably accessed and sufficient to live comfortably, and the establishment of a state-owned, not-for-profit retirement village scheme.
2. Increase funding for community spaces and the establishment of facilities, programmes, education and volunteering opportunities that are accessible to seniors.
3. Expanding housing options by building more papakāinga, prioritising kaumātua on social housing waitlists, and ensuring housing designs are suitable for their needs — single-level and warm, with mobility features and room for intergenerational living.
4. Ensure support services are grounded in cultural values, and that home and community care workers are well trained, supported and paid equitably and fairly by including travel time.
5. Resource Māori, Pacific and migrant organisations to provide kaumātua care that is aligned with their values, cultural practices and tikanga.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-small-busin.title: Small Business
documents/web-manifesto-2026-small-busin.text:
# Small Business

### Championing small, local enterprise.

**The Green Party will back local businesses, support sustainable industries and ensure small businesses have a fair shot.**

When wealth is kept in local communities, we all benefit. But too often, small businesses face an economy that is stacked against them.

In the last year, we saw the highest number of business liquidations in almost 15 years. Local suppliers are being squeezed by the supermarket duopoly, while factories are closing and costing jobs. This is the story right across our economy.

Successive governments have built an economy where large international corporates can flourish, sending immense profits offshore, while small and local businesses fight just to keep the lights on.

The Green Party will reform our economic rules to back local businesses, even the playing field, and support sustainable, low-carbon industries to thrive.

### **Our plan**

1. Revitalise ‘Buy Kiwi Made’ and expand country of origin labelling so it’s easier to support local businesses.
2. Commit government departments to buying more goods and services from Aotearoa businesses.
3. Foster sustainable, low-carbon jobs in the information and communication technology sector by expanding access to grants and rebates for smaller sized firms.
4. Continue to invest in community-led regional development with a focus on sustainable building, regenerative agriculture and horticulture, improving low-carbon infrastructure, and iwi- and hapū-led economic activity.
5. Reform competition laws to create a fairer playing field for small businesses and to benefit consumers. Increase the resources and powers of regulatory agencies to investigate anti-competitive practice.

documents/web-manifesto-2026-te-tiriti-o.title: Te Tiriti o Waitangi
documents/web-manifesto-2026-te-tiriti-o.text:
# Te Tiriti o Waitangi

### Advancing an Aotearoa that embraces Te Tiriti.

**The Green Party will put Te Tiriti o Waitangi at the heart of a modern Aotearoa founded on real partnership.**

We envision an Aotearoa where our governing structures uphold the rangatiratanga of iwi and hapū, providing dignity for all. We can achieve this by demonstrating true partnership between tangata whenua and the Crown as intended by Te Tiriti.

Successive governments have consistently breached Te Tiriti. The resulting harm, lack of accountability and denial of Māori as equal partners mean that the Crown has not upheld its side of the partnership. When Te Tiriti breaches are ongoing, apologies for past harms are not enough.

It is our responsibility to acknowledge, take accountability and put right the wrongdoings committed by the Crown. These have led to worse outcomes for Māori in too many ways. We can’t allow government to pretend that everyone is equal in this country when the exact systems that were created to oppress Māori are still operating.

The Green Party understands that He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti are the foundation for an enduring constitutional partnership. We acknowledge the need for ongoing dialogue to build the awareness, understanding and vision that will give life to Te Tiriti in Aotearoa.

### **Our plan**

1. Amend the Treaty of Waitangi Act to recognise that Te Tiriti is the authoritative text and that Te Tiriti works in conjunction with He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni.
2. Implement genuine Te Tiriti-based decision-making models across government and resource iwi and hapū to participate as partners rather than as advisors.
3. Reform the Treaty Settlements process by amending the settlement policy guide for negotiators to enable fair negotiations and just reparations without ceding sovereignty, removing any clauses that refer to ‘Full and Final settlement’, ending the ‘large natural grouping’ approach to Treaty settlements, and validating hapū rangatiratanga.
4. Increase resourcing for the Waitangi Tribunal, providing them with the power to make binding recommendations for the return of Crown and Private land to iwi, whānau and hapū.
5. Facilitate the return of whenua outside of Treaty Settlements that was wrongfully alienated from tangata whenua, including through exploring a right-of-first-refusal process that enables the return of private land to iwi, hapū and whānau at point of sale.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-tertiary-ed.title: Tertiary Education
documents/web-manifesto-2026-tertiary-ed.text:
# Tertiary Education

### Opportunities for everyone to learn and grow.

**The Green Party will support student success by overhauling tertiary education.**

We all benefit when somebody takes on tertiary study, contributing original thought and their skills to our communities, hapori (community), country and the world.

Unfortunately, successive governments have forced universities and polytechs to make deep cuts to the courses and services students need to succeed.

At the same time, they have normalised student poverty, leaving students struggling to pay the rent and eat a decent meal.

Choosing to study shouldn’t be a commitment to years of stress and hardship. Tertiary education should be the springboard into a meaningful career and the expansion of human knowledge.

The Green Party will overhaul the tertiary education sector, so our institutions are sustainable and operate in the public good.

That means a tertiary education system where it’s affordable to study, students get the support they need to succeed, and staff have good pay and working conditions so that everyone can benefit from a world-class tertiary education system.

We can ensure that we have a thriving tertiary sector that looks after students, staff and the communities they serve – because tertiary education should be for everyone.

### **Our plan**

1. Support students with a universal student income, including at postgraduate level, and ensure courses that require work placements pay students at least the living wage.
2. Overhaul funding for the tertiary sector to ensure it delivers rigorous research, a wide range of course options, quality teaching, comprehensive student services, decent pay and conditions for staff, and full participation of disabled students.
3. Empower polytechnics with adequate funding and strong local control to meet workforce and community needs, and protect courses, campuses and staff from cuts.
4. Expand free apprenticeship programmes, reduce student loan repayments and work towards fees-free tertiary education and a student debt write-off.
5. Ensure all tertiary institutes uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi and deliver equitable outcomes for ākonga Māori (Māori students). Expand the Māori and Pasifika Trades Training programme, and fully resource Whare Wānanga to increase opportunities for kaupapa Māori education.
6. Return to default student union membership and develop a governance model for tertiary organisations in which staff, students, communities and tangata whenua govern together.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-transport.m.title: Transport
documents/web-manifesto-2026-transport.m.text:
# Transport

### Easy, sustainable ways to get around.

**The Green Party will invest in modern, sustainable, and affordable transport options.**

This will make it easier and cheaper for people to safely get around our cities and regions.

Aotearoa was once joined up by buses and a reliable passenger rail system. Fast, frequent and reliable public transport ran throughout our cities and towns.

After our rail network was sold off for private profit, it was returned to the people in disarray. Successive governments have failed to invest in our rail network or plan for the future in our urban areas. Our cities are now choked with cars, instead of flourishing with people.

People have been priced out of our central cities and now live in the outskirts, where they are poorly served by public transport and don’t have safe walking and biking infrastructure. This has left so many with no option but to rely on cars to get around, adding to congestion and making people vulnerable to oil price shocks.

The Green Party will invest in transport for the future so we all have real options to get around our communities, wherever we live. We’ll ease congestion with rapid buses and surface light rail in our biggest cities. We will fund councils to build linked-up bike networks, and invest in rail to move people and freight.

Giving people the freedom to take public transport or bike instead of being forced into cars will provide them immediate relief where it counts — their wallets.

### **Our plan**

1. Transform public transport networks, including building mass rapid transit in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, and providing comprehensive bus lanes in all cities.
2. Invest in nationwide rapid rail for passengers and freight to connect regions and major cities and contribute to economic development and decarbonisation.
3. Introduce targeted subsidies for e-cargo bikes. Introduce e-bike sharing schemes in community hubs, to allow more families to save on transport costs.
4. Fund affordable, reliable, interregional rural bus services, and on-demand public transport, including by-Māori for-Māori public transport to serve kōhanga reo and rural schools.
5. Extend Community Connect to provide free fares for students and apprentices, community service card holders, everyone under 18, and all Total Mobility card holders.
6. Enable the provision of transport services publicly instead of for profit by replacing the Public Transport Operating Model.
7. Create safe walking and biking routes to all community hubs including schools through building more bike lanes and safe crossings, and lowering speed limits near schools.
8. Implement a phase-out date for the import of fossil-fuel powered vehicles, build more EV (electric vehicle) charging stations, remove regulatory barriers to EV car-sharing and re-introduce incentives for EV uptake.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-violence-pr.title: Violence Prevention
documents/web-manifesto-2026-violence-pr.text:
# Violence Prevention

### Keeping whānau and communities safe.

**The Green Party will make sure everyone can live a life free from violence and heal from trauma.**

Our homes, whānau and communities should be places of aroha, care and safety — free from fear and harm.

Aotearoa has among the highest rates of intimate partner violence, sexual violence and child abuse. This disproportionately harms people in vulnerable professions and communities, and can have long-lasting impacts that are passed down through families.

The current Government has stalled progress on work initiated by the Green Party to prevent violence from happening. They have failed to deliver action, instead cutting funding to critical community-led services.

The Green Party will invest in stopping violence before it starts. Our approach will be safe, accessible and integrated, building on people’s strength and with Te Tiriti o Waitangi at its heart. We will mobilise our communities to help and ensure our workforce is skilled and culturally competent.

New Zealanders deserve a government who are committed to ending violence in Aotearoa. We will invest in tailored specialist and whānau-centred services for victims and survivors focused on prevention, healing, recovery and restoration. This includes services to support those who have used violence to take accountability and change their behaviour.

The Green Party vision is an Aotearoa where everyone feels safe and supported.

### **Our plan**

1. Fund the implementation of the action plan for Te Aorerekura: National Strategy to Eliminate Family Violence and Sexual Violence, centred on Te Tiriti.
2. Resource kaupapa Māori solutions and community-led solutions to family and sexual violence, that have have been developed by disproportionately impacted groups, including women, Pasifika, rainbow, and disabled communities.
3. Prioritise violence responses and prevention by improving workforce and broader public understanding of the drivers and signs of violence, and how to respond in ways that enhance safety and healing.
4. Amend the Crimes Act to criminalise coercive control, amend the definition of consent, and preclude a defence of reluctant consent to affirm that consent must be free and voluntary, and can be withdrawn at any time while ensuring these changes cause no further harm.
5. Restore relationship and sexuality teaching guidelines — including education on healthy relationships, diverse identities and sexualities, and affirmative consent — in all schools.
6. Increase funding for counselling and mental health support for victims, whānau, witnesses, defendants and legal professionals engaging in the justice system.

[< Back to Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

documents/web-manifesto-2026-welfare-of-.title: Welfare of Animals
documents/web-manifesto-2026-welfare-of-.text:
# Welfare of Animals

### Caring for all animals that call Aotearoa home.

**The Green Party will keep animals safe from cruelty and suffering.**

Animals should live a happy, comfortable life free from suffering.

Unfortunately, the Luxon Government has let big industry players write our animal welfare laws, putting corporate greed ahead of the wellbeing of animals.

Thousands of farmed animals are suffering unnecessarily because the standards that are meant to protect their safety aren’t being upheld. Cruel and harmful practices are allowed to continue.

The Green Party will protect animals from practices that put profit ahead of their welfare. We have been the parliamentary champion for animal welfare for decades.

In recent years, we have fought for and protected the ban on live exports at sea and won the end to greyhound racing. We have been the leading parliamentary voice against mud farming, cruel imports and the caging of mother pigs.

The Green Party will transform our animal welfare protections to make Aotearoa a place where all animals are treated with care and respect.

We will prioritise ethical treatment so that all animals can live a good life no matter where they live — on farms, in our homes or in the wild.

### **Our plan**

1. Create a new Commissioner for Animals to independently monitor and advocate for the rights of animals, and an independent ministry.
2. Resource the National Animal Welfare Advisory Committee to ensure all animal welfare codes genuinely comply with the Animal Welfare Act, and introduce stronger codes for farmed animals.
3. Phase out harmful activities including debeaking of hens, intensive winter grazing, factory farming, octopus farming, farrowing crates and rodeo.
4. Require that imported products meet the animal welfare standards of Aotearoa, including for cosmetics.
5. Introduce consistent, clear and enforceable standards for manufacturing claims about animal welfare and ingredients (such as ‘free range’, ‘cruelty free’ and ‘vegan’).
6. Retain the ban on live exports of farmed animals by sea and extend the ban to include live exports of farmed animals by air and wild-caught animals such as endangered tuna longfin eels.

# Workforce rights

### Employment protections and decent pay for all workers.

**The Green Party will protect rights, improve conditions and make things fairer for workers.**

Work should provide dignity, security and a fair share in the prosperity we create together. Strong employment rights, decent pay and collective voice are essential for a thriving economy and a healthy democracy.

Workers should be valued for their contribution, protected from exploitation and supported to live well — not just survive.

Right now, too many people are locked into insecure, low-paid or unsafe work. Employers hold the balance of power and unemployment is used to suppress workers’ fair expectations for better pay and conditions.

The current Government has launched a sustained attack on workers’ rights — removing pay equity and fair pay agreements, cutting health and safety protections, and normalising insecurity. Meanwhile, industries producing important goods for Aotearoa are forced to close when international corporations aren’t happy with their bottom line.

The Green Party will implement a workforce system built on fairness, democracy and care, restoring the balance between workers and employers. This means standing up for pay equity, safe workplaces and secure employment.

We will undo this Government’s attacks on workers and build strong, future-focused employment protections. Our plan will support a flourishing economy that works for everyone — through the transition to a sustainable zero carbon economy.

### **Our plan**

1. Strengthen worker bargaining power by changing employment law to default union membership. This means people automatically join a union when they start a new job, but can opt out later.
2. Expand the right to strike, including for breaches of collective agreements and political and solidarity reasons.
3. Strengthen employment law to protect all workers’ free time with a right to disconnect. Ensure protection from unwanted contact or surveillance out of working hours.
4. Explore legislating to put workers’ representatives on boards of publicly listed companies.
5. Guarantee annual minimum wage increases that at least keep up with inflation. Pay all publicly funded roles a living wage. Work towards matching the minimum wage to the living wage.
6. Increase paid parental leave to 15 months for the primary caregiver, with additional ring-fenced leave for partners, while also increasing payments.
7. Protect platform and gig-economy workers by strengthening the test for whether a worker is a contractor.
8. Close the gender and ethnic pay gaps by undoing the Government’s changes to the pay equity regime and resuming claims, pay transparency measures, and comprehensive pay gap reporting.

# Zero Waste

### Building a sustainable circular economy.

**The Green Party will take action to reduce waste and protect the environment from pollution.**

In a truly sustainable system, nature is protected rather than treated as a dumping ground. We can build a circular economy where waste is designed out and resources are valued and reused.

Under the current Government, progress towards our zero-waste future has stalled. Action on plastic pollution has ground to a halt, and funding for solutions has dried up. Corporations continue to make products that won’t last or can’t be repaired, filling up our landfills. Communities are left to deal with the pollution and impacts.

The Green Party has shown what’s possible. In government, we banned single-use plastic bags and reduced food waste going to landfill. We increased the waste levy for the first time in over a decade and introduced mandatory product stewardship schemes. We also started work on a container return scheme.

We will build on this legacy by holding corporations accountable for the waste they create. This means both reducing waste, and requiring the recovery, recycling, reuse and redistribution of materials.

By supporting communities to lead local solutions, we will accelerate the transition to a sustainable and circular economy that allows people and nature to thrive.

### **Our plan**

1. Establish strong product policy measures, including mandatory product stewardship, a beverage container return scheme, phase-outs of problematic products and comprehensive right-to-repair.
2. Direct revenue from the waste disposal levy into waste minimisation initiatives and stop diverting the local government portion to other purposes. Increase the levy to match international best practice and apply a consistent rate across all landfill classes.
3. Introduce a moratorium on waste-to-energy plants and explore energy generation from biogas associated with animal and plant wastes.
4. Build on proposed reforms of the Waste Minimisation Act to implement timely, binding, measurable and ambitious waste reduction targets. Ensure legislation gives effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Introduce comprehensive duty-of-care systems for the waste and resource recovery sector covering all waste streams, including hazardous waste.
5. Make greater use of discarded soil. Divert soil from landfills, where safe and appropriate to do so.
6. Prioritise local, mana whenua and community-driven solutions to resource recovery, implementation of national zero-waste strategies, and organic waste reduction, diversion and processing.

THE GREEN PARTY

# Manifesto 2026

#### A Green government.

#### **FOR ALL OF US.**

[Manifesto 2026](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026)

[View contents](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026#manifesto_2026_grid)

[Read as a PDF](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_full)

[Our Māori Manifesto](https://www.greens.org.nz/maori_manifesto_2026_full)

Our vision is an Aotearoa that honours Te Tiriti o Waitangi, where power and wealth sit with our communities, and where people and the rest of nature thrive together.

**Aotearoa has enough for all of us**. Our government should work for people and planet, not the greed of corporations and their shareholders.

For the past three years we’ve seen a Government on the side of the super-rich and the most powerful corporations.

Climate action cut, protections for nature gutted, and decisions handed to lobbyists and donors while families struggle with power bills, rent and groceries.

We’ve been told our entire lives that a fairer country is impossible by those profiting from things staying exactly as they are: unequal and unfair.

But New Zealanders know better. Politics belongs to those who turn up, and in communities across the motu, people are turning up demanding action.

This manifesto is our plan for a Green government to harness the energy for change, built on three priorities: affordable living, healthy nature and real democracy.

Affordable living, because we can have affordable electricity, housing, transport and groceries if we take on mega-corporate profits, and only the Green Party are willing to do that.

Healthy nature, because since the beginning we have worked to protect and restore our water, forests, air and soil. And real democracy, because laws should be made for regular New Zealanders, not those who can afford to buy access to shape the rules in their favour.

Paid for by a plan that will tax the super-rich and mega-corporations, help fund critical social services, and cut income tax for 96 percent of people.

None of this would be possible without the hopes, ideas and passion of Green Party members, and the movement they’ve built. This manifesto is their work, and their commitment to change in Aotearoa.

That change is not hypothetical. Last time the Greens were in Government, we took more action on climate than the previous three decades of governments combined, secured the biggest ever boost to funding for protecting native plants and wildlife, and delivered Aotearoa’s first plan to eliminate family and sexual violence.

A party vote for the Green Party puts more Green MPs and Ministers around the decision-making table to reverse the damage from the last three years and fix the rules so they’re on side of people and planet.

Outlined in this document is a plan to do what is necessary. Protect what we all love. Ensure everyone’s needs are met. And make life better for all of us here in Aotearoa.

## Summary

Te Ao Tūroa helps us to care for all coastal and aquatic ecosystems through active kaitiakitanga practice and precautionary, adaptive, integrated stewardship. Doing all we can to support a naturally regenerating ocean is essential to protect its health, provide for us, and assist climate stability. The Green Party will promote Te Tiriti-based governance of the seas of Aotearoa New Zealand to regenerate mauri, prevent damage from human activities, increase resilience to climate change, and support the thriving marine ecosystems that underpin a healthy, well-managed blue economy.

OUR VISION

> The ocean’s life force and life-supporting capacity are vibrant and vigorous. All human relationships with the marine realm are mutually regenerative.

## Values and Principles

##### Honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Kaitiakitanga, led by tangata whenua, should guide human relationships with the sea, ensuring that it is better cared for. Māori regard all life forms within Te Ao Tūroa as taonga that require appropriate consideration through kawa and tikanga.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Protecting the mauri, mana, and tapu - the intrinsic vitality, potency, and sanctity of the ocean and of all who dwell within and around it - is fundamental to the enduring life-support system of planet Earth.

##### Social Responsibility:

We should equitably provide for the sustainable livelihoods and recreational and spiritual opportunities valued by New Zealanders that healthy oceans and coasts offer.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

A range of interests at both local and national levels must guide decisions concerning coastal and marine management. Decisions must include consideration of the needs of future generations and of the wider environment and ecology.

##### Non-violence:

Human activity should be restorative, not harmful, to the intrinsic mauri, mana, and tapu of all life in the marine environment.

##### Urgency:

Given the biodiversity crisis, the declining health of ocean ecosystems, and climate change impacts such as acidification and increasing sea temperatures, significant increases in investment and pace of implementation are urgently needed to regenerate coastal and marine ecosystems.

##### Interconnection:

Ki uta ki tai - from the mountains to the sea. Marine management requires integrated management of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, including the vital role of  wetlands in coastal and estuarine zones. The health of people, land, and oceans are inextricably linked.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“All our waters will be in transition to becoming clean and able to support healthy ecosystems.
All native species and their habitats will be thriving or on a path to recovery in terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments.
Our laws and practices will respect the biological integrity of all life while prioritising the health of indigenous species and ecosystems.
The customary and decision-making roles of whānau, hapū, and iwi will be integral to decisions about resource use.
Decision-making about resource use will provide for community participation and environmental justice.”
Actions from this policy that work toward these goals include:

- Establish a well-resourced and politically independent Ocean Commission to develop and establish Te Tiriti-based ocean governance of the entire marine area, including the Exclusive Economic Zone, and advise the Government on legislative, policy, and institutional reform. (1.1)
- Reform fisheries and marine protection legislation, including establishing a national, comprehensive, and coherent system of no-take marine protected areas. (2.1.1)
- Supporting the use of marine cultural health indices, shaped by mātauranga Māori, to inform policy, management, and operations. (2.1.4)
- Ending bottom trawling, prioritising seamounts and areas with high levels of sequestered carbon and biodiversity for protection. (5.1.2)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64850/attachments/original/1778624610/Policy-Greens_Marine_Policy_2022-2026.pdf)

## Connected Policies

This policy is one of several that focus on [Biodiversity and Environmental Regeneration](https://www.greens.org.nz/biodiversity_environmental_regeneration_policy), alongside [Freshwater](https://www.greens.org.nz/freshwater_policy) and [Land Use and Soils](https://www.greens.org.nz/land_use_and_soils_policy). The mauri of the oceans is connected to human activity on land, notably [Agriculture](https://www.greens.org.nz/agriculture_policy), [Forestry](https://www.greens.org.nz/forestry_policy), [Housing and Sustainable Communities](https://www.greens.org.nz/housing_policy), and [Waste and Hazardous Substances](https://www.greens.org.nz/waste_and_hazardous_substances_policy). [Climate Change](https://www.greens.org.nz/climate_change_policy) also impacts marine health. For acute marine crisis response, see our [Emergency Management](https://www.greens.org.nz/emergency_management_policy) Policy. See also our policies on coastal [Transport](https://www.greens.org.nz/transport_policy) and wave and tidal [Energy](https://www.greens.org.nz/energy_policy).

# Media Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/media_policy#media_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64864/attachments/original/1778624610/Policy-Greens_Media_Policy_2014-2026.pdf)

## Summary

The Green Party will support an independent media and enable community-based media. We will support publicly owned broadcasting services and fund locally produced content, prioritising those communities that are not well served by commercial interests, including Māori and children.

OUR VISION

> A strong, diverse and independent media contributes to the maintenance of effective democracy, and to our social, cultural, economic and environmental wellbeing.

## Values and Principles

Decisions relating to broadcasting and media must uphold the following values and principles:

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Māori media should be prioritised and recognised as a platform to uphold the culture of tangata whenua in Aotearoa New Zealand.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

The environmental impact of the production and storage of media content should be minimised.

##### Social Responsibility:

The media should be accessible to people of all abilities, and used to inform, educate and entertain in a manner that supports citizens to participate effectively in democracy and appreciate each others’ needs, interests and aspirations.

##### Appropriate Decision-Making:

The right to broadcast or publish is balanced with expectations to act in a responsible and inclusive manner.

##### Non-Violence:

Non-violent resolution of political and social conflict is based on the knowledge, acceptance and understanding of diverse communities, and of their needs, interests and aspirations. Media should act as a means of checks and balances against the misuse or abuse of social, economic and political power.

##### Independence:

A vigorous, independent and diverse media is the cornerstone of a free society: Public broadcasting and community-based media initiatives should be supported; and directives by the state, or ownership and control by international media conglomerates, or domination by local commercial monopolies should be avoided.

## Strategic Priorities

The Green Party’s strategic goals include:
“As a Party we want to see Te Ao Māori and Te Reo Māori flourish in Aotearoa.
“All people will be empowered to shape the systems that affect them.”
Actions in this policy that will help achieve this include:

- Establish, monitor and enforce obligations attached to the right to broadcast and stream content online, including honouring the rights and interests of tangata whenua under Te Tiriti o Waitangi. (1.1)
- Support quality public service broadcasting and streaming, and digital media commons, that nurture and promote our own talent and creativity as a nation, reflecting the unique social and cultural diversity of Aotearoa New Zealand. (1.3)

- Protect the political independence and public ownership of Radio New Zealand, Television New Zealand and the Mãori Television Service and iwi radio. (1.3.2)
- Secure long term funding and support for dedicated Māori language media, including the Māori Television Service and iwi radio stations, to be independent, secure and successfully play a major role in revitalising language and culture. (2.4.2)

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64864/attachments/original/1778624610/Policy-Greens_Media_Policy_2014-2026.pdf)

## Connected Policies

A freely available and politically independent media makes a significant contribution to the effectiveness of [Governance](https://www.greens.org.nz/governance_policy), [Research, Science and Technology](https://www.greens.org.nz/research_science_and_technology_policy), and [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/education_policy), through the provision of political debate, diverse perspectives and information about the world we live in. It is a key mechanism for celebrating the [Arts, Culture and Heritage](https://www.greens.org.nz/arts_culture_and_heritage_policy) of Aotearoa New Zealand. It is increasingly entwined with the development of [Digital](https://www.greens.org.nz/digital_policy) technologies. Its [Workforce](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy) must be protected.

[Back to News](https://www.greens.org.nz/news)

# NZ must pursue independent foreign policy

Posted at November 07, 2024 11:46 AM by
[Teanau Tuiono](https://www.greens.org.nz/Teanau_Tuiono)

Related Articles

[Democracy and International relations](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_democracy_and_international_relations)
[Foreign Affairs](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_foreign_affairs)
[Teanau Tuiono](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_teanau_tuiono)

The Green Party says the need is greater than ever for Aotearoa New Zealand to pursue an independent foreign policy.

“The US election result should be a wake-up call that our country must steer clear of the AUKUS military pact,” says the Green Party Foreign Affairs Spokesperson Teanau Tuiono.

“We cannot be hustled into a military alliance with the US, especially when it’s about to be led by a volatile firebrand with fascist leanings who cozies up to autocrats and dictators, and attacks the rights of women, immigrants, rainbow communities and the most vulnerable.

“Aotearoa New Zealand must return to the independent and principled approach to foreign affairs that we were valued for in the international community. We should use that position to advance climate action, protect nature, advocate for indigenous and human rights, and global justice.

“Advocating for, and working towards, peaceful solutions to the world’s conflicts must be an absolute priority for our country. Unfortunately, this Government is jeopardising our independent foreign policy voice and falling into line behind a march to conflict and great power antagonism that is reckless and unnecessary.

“The current, unstable geopolitical environment calls for cool heads. We should not be entering into any pillar of the AUKUS framework. Even if Pillar 2 is the so-called technology-only part of the agreement, it is still part of the same precarious project fixated on conflict with the west’s perceived enemies.

“The US involvement in the atrocities in Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East should serve as a warning to us that tying ourselves to the military projects of a state that allows or facilitates indiscriminate attacks on civilian populations is unacceptable.

“Let’s remain an advocate for diplomacy and dialogue, and pursue our independent voice in world affairs. That’s what other countries look to us for,” says Teanau Tuiono.

# Overseas New Zealanders Policy

[View our Priorities](https://www.greens.org.nz/overseas_new_zealanders_policy#overseas_new_zealanders_policy_strategic_priorities)
[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64878/attachments/original/1778624611/Policy-Greens_Overseas_New_Zealanders_Policy_2022-2026.pdf)

## Summary

This policy covers: Te Tiriti o Waitangi and the Aotearoa New Zealand Diaspora; Services, Support and Human Rights; Meaningful Connections; and Participation in Society.

OUR VISION

> The Green Party celebrates the large and diverse diaspora of Aotearoa New Zealand, fosters mutually-beneficial and meaningful links to home, and safeguards our rights and well-being.

## Values and Principles

Waiho i te toipoto, kaua i te toiroa
Let us keep close together, not far apart
This policy is grounded in the Green Party charter, international Green values and elementary policies of fairness, equity and human rights.

##### Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi:

Tangata whenua should lead all kaupapa related to Māori living overseas.

##### Ecological Wisdom:

Overseas New Zealanders should be supported with sustainable and environmentally-conscious connections with home.

##### Social Responsibility:

Overseas New Zealanders should have human rights, democratic rights and access to the principles of citizenship, regardless of where we live.

##### Appropriate decision-making:

Overseas New Zealanders should have the opportunity to contribute to our home country and have their voices heard.

##### Non-violence:

States have a basic duty of care to their citizens. This must include overseas New Zealanders and be free of political bias, favouritism or status based on perceived worth to our home country.

Full Policy Link

[View the Full Policy](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/64878/attachments/original/1778624611/Policy-Greens_Overseas_New_Zealanders_Policy_2022-2026.pdf)

The Aotearoa New Zealand diaspora is impacted by policy in several areas including [Governance](https://www.greens.org.nz/governance_policy), [Disability](https://www.greens.org.nz/disability_policy), [Health](https://www.greens.org.nz/health_policy), [Global Affairs](https://www.greens.org.nz/global_affairs_policy), [Immigration](https://www.greens.org.nz/immigration_policy), [Livelihoods](https://www.greens.org.nz/livelihoods_policy), [Education](https://www.greens.org.nz/tertiary_education_policy), [Te Tiriti o Waitangi](https://www.greens.org.nz/te_tiriti_policy), and [Workforce](https://www.greens.org.nz/workforce_policy).

# People and nature first in Greens’ rivers and oceans policy

Posted at July 06, 2026 1:45 PM by

[Chlöe Swarbrick](https://www.greens.org.nz/Chloe_Swarbrick)
 and
[Marama Davidson](https://www.greens.org.nz/Marama_Davidson)

Related Articles

[Nature and Climate](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_nature_and_climate)
[Conservation](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_conservation)
[Environment](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_environment)
[Oceans and Fisheries](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_oceans_and_fisheries)
[Chlöe Swarbrick](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_chloe_swarbrick)
[Marama Davidson](https://www.greens.org.nz/news_marama_davidson)

The Green Party is calling foul on the Luxon Government’s dismantling of environmental protection, announcing a policy programme to deliver clean drinking water, swimmable rivers and beaches, and healthy oceans for all New Zealanders.

“This is about protecting our taiao. The Green Party has announced its policy programme ‘Drink Swim Fish’ which will deliver far reaching environmental change and protect human and ecological health from harm caused by corporate greed,” says Green Party Co-leader Marama Davidson.

“Clean, healthy water is a human right, and has been a way of life in Aotearoa for many generations.

“But that way of life has been taken from today’s generations by weak rules that allow industrial scale exploitation. It is madness that in Aotearoa, up to 100,000 people become sick from unsafe drinking water every year, popular beaches and swimming spots are closed every summer, and our once common fish like our iconic tarakihi populations have been fished to the brink of collapse.

“The Green Party’s policy package will reverse the widespread degradation of our environment, and protect human and ecological health from corporate greed,” says Marama.

**Among eight policy interventions, the Green Party will:**

- Protect drinking water by setting strong environmental limits and lowering nitrate limits.
- Protect rivers and coasts by strengthening rules for wastewater discharges.
- Protect our moana by phasing out destructive bottom trawling.

Green Party Co-leader Chlöe Swarbrick says “There is no economy without the environment. When the Government fails to protect our environment we all pay the price in clean-up costs, in our people and animals getting sick, let alone the impact on our economy.”

“Safe drinking water, a swim at the local beach, and catching some snapper on the weekend should not be too much to ask in this beautiful country.

“The recent outpouring of love for both public conservation land and our fish – against Luxon’s Government’s plans – have only reaffirmed that New Zealanders want environmental health prioritised over commercial profits. It’s in our nature.

“Only the Green Party will fix the rules so the health of our communities and environment always come first. New Zealanders can be sure this would mean all of us can drink, swim, and fish in the places we love,” says Chlöe.

For more info, visit [Drink, Swim Fish - Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand.](https://www.greens.org.nz/waterforlife)
